feat(web): a return path that cannot leave this site (#564)

Sign-in is reached from somewhere and has to send the member back. That is a
`next` parameter, and a `next` parameter is the one place where being
approximately right is an open redirect.

The check is on the SHAPE of the string rather than on a parsed URL, because
`new URL(raw, origin)` resolves `//evil.example` against this origin, reports
it as valid, and hands back another site. It begins with a slash, so every
test anybody writes in a hurry passes it.

Refused, with a case each: an absolute URL; a relative path, whose meaning
depends on where it is read; `//host` and `/\host`, both protocol-relative
once a browser has normalised the backslash; anything carrying a control
character, which is how a URL gets split; and this flow's own `/auth/...`
routes, where landing after finishing a sign-in is a loop rather than a
return.

A refusal is never an error. Somebody arriving with a mangled parameter still
wants to sign in, so they sign in and land on the fallback.

Also here because they are the same subject: the outcomes a redirect can hand
the sign-in page, and the absolute URL an auth provider is configured to send
somebody back to. It carries the language, because that route has none of its
own and a failure needs explaining in the language being read.

The module joins vitest.config.ts's coverage list in the same commit. A logic
file left off that list escapes the gate silently, which is worse than not
having one.
MSGEOF
git add web/src/lib/member/strings.ts web/src/lib/member/strings.test.ts "web/src/pages/[lang]/signin.astro" "web/src/pages/[lang]/signin.test.ts" web/src/pages/auth/confirm.ts && git commit -q -F - <<'MSGEOF'
feat(web): the sign-in page sends a link, and the link signs a member in (#564)

The email path of the design board's two, wired without changing what the
page promises. `signInWithOtp` sends it; /auth/confirm exchanges what comes
back for the same @supabase/ssr cookie session the editorial sign-in
produces. A first link creates the account, so signing up and signing in are
one act and there is no second screen to build.

No password, and therefore no reset, no strength meter and no breach response
for stored credentials. The board draws no password field and the shell note
rules one out in as many words.

/auth/confirm accepts BOTH shapes a provider might send - a token_hash to
verify, or a PKCE code to exchange - because which one arrives depends on the
project's email template, and a route that handles one and answers 500 to the
other works on the deployment it was written against and fails on the next.
It narrows the OTP type rather than casting it: `recovery` is deliberately
off the list, since this product never asks for a password and so never sends
one, which makes a recovery link arriving here something that did not come
from us.

It renders nothing and has no language of its own, so it hands an outcome to
the page that does. A member who clicked a link in their mail gets a sentence
rather than a stack trace, whatever went wrong.

The POST renders instead of redirecting. Post/redirect/get would cost the
address that was typed, and "a link is on its way to <the address you typed>"
is exactly the sentence somebody who mistyped it needs; the form stays under
it so they can correct it.

The shell path stays disabled, and the panel beside both paths now speaks for
that one alone. Standing next to a form that works and saying neither path
does would be the same dishonesty it was written to prevent.

signin.test.ts and strings.test.ts are rewritten rather than relaxed. They
asserted no form, no method, no action, three disabled controls and copy
carrying no URL, and they were right to: that was the promise. The new
promise is pinned as tightly - there is a form and it posts, the shell button
is still natively disabled, no state renders a password field, an
unconfigured deployment says so and sends nothing, and an outcome the page
has no sentence for renders nothing at all rather than the word. The rule
about passwords moved rather than lapsed: the word may appear only in a
sentence that denies one.
MSGEOF

F1 of [the cashback frontend brief](https://github.com/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/blob/main/docs/master-prompts/cashback-frontend.md). The sign-in page drew the two paths the design board draws and printed on its own face that neither was wired. One of them works now, and the page promises exactly what it did before minus that sentence.

### An email link, and never a password

`signInWithOtp` sends it. `/auth/confirm` exchanges what comes back for the same `@supabase/ssr` cookie session the editorial sign-in produces. **A first link creates the account**, so signing up and signing in are one act — which is why the register page changes in the same PR rather than being left telling the only untrue story on the site.

No password means no reset screen, no strength meter, and no breach response for stored credentials. The board draws no password field and the shell note rules one out in as many words.

### `/auth/confirm` accepts both shapes a provider might send

`?token_hash=&type=` to verify, or a PKCE `?code=` to exchange. Which one arrives depends on the project's email template and the flow the SDK negotiated, and a route that handles one and answers 500 to the other works on the deployment it was written against and fails on the next — a configuration trap rather than a route.

It narrows the OTP type rather than casting it. `recovery` is deliberately **not** on the accepted list: the provider would verify one, and this product never asks for a password and so never sends one, which makes a recovery link arriving here something that did not come from us.

It renders nothing and has no language of its own, so it hands an outcome to the page that does. A member who clicked a link in their mail gets a sentence, not a stack trace.

### The return path

`safeReturnPath` is its own module with its own tests, because a `next` parameter is the one place where being approximately right is an open redirect. The check is on the **shape of the string**, not on a parsed URL: `new URL('//evil.example', origin)` resolves to another origin and reports it as valid, and it starts with a slash, so it passes every test written in a hurry.

Refused, with a case each: absolute URLs; relative paths; `//host` and `/\\host` (both protocol-relative once a browser normalises the backslash); control characters, which is how a URL gets split; and this flow's own `/auth/…` routes, where landing after finishing a sign-in is a loop rather than a return. A refusal is never an error — somebody with a mangled parameter still wants to sign in.

### The POST renders instead of redirecting

Post/redirect/get would cost the address the member typed, and *"a link is on its way to <the address you typed>"* is exactly the sentence somebody who mistyped it needs. The form stays under it so they can correct it.

### What is still owed, and what stopped being owed

The shell button is still natively `disabled`. The panel beside both paths now speaks for **that one alone** — standing next to a form that works and saying neither path does would be the same dishonesty it was written to prevent, pointing the other way.

The front page's control becomes a link, carrying the page the reader was on. It was a disabled button whose state the sign-in page quoted as current truth; the two could not stop agreeing on different days. `signInPending` and `frontPageButtonState` retire with it.

The register page loses three disabled fields — one of them a password, and a disabled field is still a promise about what is coming — and its sentence about an auth provider that "is not connected yet", which also named the vendor three lines from a module that goes to some length not to. It keeps the halves that work: the places to follow, and the dated consent record per purpose (FR-011).

### The tests were rewritten, not relaxed

`signin.test.ts` asserted no `<form>`, no `method=`, no `action=`, three disabled controls and no `/auth/` href. That was the right test for the promise the page made. The new promise is pinned as tightly: there is a form and it posts; the shell button is still natively disabled; **no state renders a password field**; an unconfigured deployment says so and disables the field; an outcome the page has no sentence for renders nothing rather than the word; a `next` it would not honour never reaches the markup.

`member/strings.test.ts` forbade any URL, `mailto:` or `http` in the catalogue — the rule that kept copy from describing a mechanism that did not exist. The email path describes one now, so the rule **moved rather than lapsed**: the word for a password may appear only in a sentence that denies one.

- `npm run check` — 0 errors, on the final commit and on the intermediate one
- `npm test` — 963 passing, coverage 94.9% statements / 94.2% branches / 90.2% functions. `src/lib/astro-url-scheme.test.ts` times out under full-suite load on this Windows machine; with `--testTimeout=30000` all 963 pass, and an unmodified `origin/main` worktree fails the same two. - `npm run build` — clean
- brand-literal lint — `no unaccounted brand literals` on a clean worktree
- `lint-refs.sh` on the branch and over the range, `lint-commit-authors.sh` over the range

### Not proved here

The link itself has not been sent by a real provider from this branch: that needs the nonprod project's keys on a deployment. It is the first thing to check on QA once this and #544 are in, and the brief's finish line depends on it."""

content.text:
Three PRs are open and fully green. Here's where things stand.

## What I found first

The master prompt isn't in your checkout — this branch is ~30 commits behind and `xcoder/member-signin` is already merged (PR #531). I read the brief from `origin/main` and started every branch fresh from there.

Then a survey turned up something the brief didn't predict: **`types.ts` had drifted far enough from the Go handlers to break a screen**. `PayoutDestination.details` — which `withdraw.astro` prints on every destination and every past withdrawal — has never been sent by the api. The handler says so in as many words: *"There is no details field and there never will be."* Against any real deployment that screen renders `undefined`. `EntryState` also carried a `declined` nothing produces and was missing `reserved`, which does arrive.

That reordered the work: the contract had to come first.

## Shipped

| PR | What | CI |
|---|---|---|
| [#561](https://github.com/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/pull/561) | The cashback types say what the api actually sends (closes #554) | green |
| [#563](https://github.com/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/pull/563) | The session belongs to whoever is signed in, and resolves where they sign in (closes #562) | green |
| [#565](https://github.com/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/pull/565) | **Member sign-in: the email path** (closes #564), stacked on #563 | green |

**#565 is F1's core.** `signInWithOtp` sends a link; `/auth/confirm` exchanges it for the same `@supabase/ssr` session the editor sign-in produces. A first link creates the account, so sign-up and sign-in are one act. No password anywhere — which is also why there's no reset screen to build. The confirm route accepts both a `token_hash` and a PKCE `code`, because which one arrives depends on the project's email template and I couldn't verify that without the Supabase keys.

The shell button stays disabled with its copy, as the design requires. The front page's button became a link, and `register.astro` stopped claiming registration was pending — it had a disabled *password* field, which this product has decided never to have.

Tests were rewritten, not relaxed. `signin.test.ts` asserted "no form, no method, no action"; it now asserts the new promise just as tightly, including that no state renders a password field.

## Also filed

- **#556** — `GET /ops/withdrawals` is called by the operator queue and isn't implemented. Same shape as #545; the queue is fixture-only until it lands.
- **#557** — `openapi.json` declares no `Problem` extensions, while the contract and the withdrawal screen both rely on `threshold`/`shortfall`.
- **#132** — added evidence that `astro-url-scheme.test.ts` times out under full-suite load. I verified this on an unmodified `origin/main` worktree before attributing it to load rather than my changes; with `--testTimeout=30000` all 963 tests pass.

## Not proved

The link has never been sent by a real provider from this branch — that needs the nonprod keys on a deployment. It's the first thing to check on QA once #565 and #544 land.

## Next, if you want me to continue

F1.4 (the flag-gated shell exchange, which is what unblocks the browser test), F2 gating, F3 opt-in plus the `/{lang}/terms` route, then F7's payout-destination screen. Worth knowing: the design canvas draws **neither** an opt-in screen nor a payout-destination form — I checked all 26 boards. Those two are mine to design, and I've noted it so it isn't rediscovered later.

content.text:
All three are `clean`, and I verified the fully-merged result builds and passes before answering.

## Merge order

```
1.  #561  The cashback types say what the api actually sends       base: main
2.  #563  The session belongs to whoever is signed in              base: main
3.  #565  Member sign-in: the email path                           base: #563's branch
```

**#561 and #563 are independent** — either can go first. **#565 must come after #563**; it's stacked on it, and GitHub will retarget it to `main` automatically when #563 merges.

I put #561 first because it fixes a screen that is broken today: `withdraw.astro` renders `destination.details`, a field the api has never sent, so against QA it prints `undefined` on every destination and every past withdrawal.

**Verified, not assumed:** I built a scratch worktree at `main + #561 + #563 + #565` and ran it — 0 typecheck errors, 969 tests passing, clean build, `no unaccounted brand literals`. Four files are touched by both #561 and #563 (`wallet.astro`, `withdraw.astro`, `ops/withdrawals.astro`, `OpsLayout.astro`); they merge cleanly in either order.

## The backend gaps — confirmed closed, and they matter

| | State | What it changes for the frontend |
|---|---|---|
| **B1** #544 | closed | `POST /api/v1/account` → `{id, email, display_name, role}`. F1.3 is now buildable for real. Two refusals to handle: a token with no email claim, and an email already held by another account. |
| **B2** #545 | closed | `GET /catalogue` landed with **exactly** the shape `api.catalogue()` already calls — `lang` required, repeatable `place`, `q`/`limit`/`cursor`, `{items, next_cursor}`. F4 collapses from "wire it" to "verify it and read `next_cursor`". |
| **B4** #546 | closed | Landed as `only /api/v1/* goes to the api` — the option we picked. The web's own `/api/cashback/clickout` now reaches the web on Hetzner, so F5 is provable on QA. |
| **B5** #547 | closed | The web gets `BRAND_DIR`, so F3's opt-in can read the terms version on QA. |
| **B6** #548 | **open** | Payout-destination verification. Expected — the brief says it isn't needed before the first transaction. |

Still open from what I filed: **#556** (`GET /ops/withdrawals` is called by the operator queue and isn't implemented — same shape as #545) and **#557** (`Problem` extensions missing from `openapi.json`).

Main has moved 23 commits but touched **nothing under `web/`**, so no rebase is needed on any of the three.

## After you merge

happened. An address already belonging to another account is something they
can act on and the sentence says what to try instead; an account that could
not be made is about the deployment and promises nothing.

An unreachable api lands with the successes, deliberately. A preview has no
api at all and a container can be restarting; neither is a reason to refuse
somebody the session they have just proved they are entitled to.

only checking for an error, so the two paths meet at one place and the

body = """Closes #567. Builds on #544, which landed the endpoint.

**A session is not an account.** #565 wired the email link, so a member signs in and holds a verified token. The api still does not know them: every cashback route looks the caller up in `account` and answers 401 when there is no row (FR-023). A member who got that far and no further would find the wallet, the catalogue and the click-out all failing while nothing about the page looked broken — the worst of the three states, because signed-out is legible and broken is legible and this is neither.

`/auth/confirm` is the one moment the web holds a fresh token **and** knows the sign-in just succeeded, which makes it the only place `POST /api/v1/account` belongs. It registers once, straight after the exchange.

### The outcomes are not all the same, and that is the work

| api says | what happens |
|---|---|
| **201** / **200** | the account exists. Onward to wherever they were headed. |
| **409** the address belongs to another account | session dropped, and the sign-in page says what to try instead |
| **400** the token carries no email | session dropped, and the page says an account could not be made |
| **401** / **500** / unreachable / no api configured | **onward anyway** |

The two middle rows drop the session rather than keep it. A member holding a session that 401s everywhere cannot tell that from a broken site, and signing in again is the move they would try regardless — so the page they land on tells them which of the two happened. One of those they can act on; the other is about the deployment and promises nothing.

The last row lands with the successes deliberately. A pull-request preview has no api at all and a container can be restarting; neither is a reason to refuse somebody the session they have just proved they are entitled to.

### Shape

`registerAccount` is a module with its own tests rather than six lines inside a route, because the outcome mapping is the whole substance. It takes no request body — the subject and the email come out of the verified token, which is the only place they can honestly come from; a body would be a client asserting an identity the token already proves.

**It never throws**, and that is the point rather than a courtesy: it runs immediately after a sign-in that has already succeeded, and a failure here must not undo one.

Both exchange shapes (`token_hash` and PKCE `code`) now read the access token out of what they returned rather than only checking for an error, so the two paths meet at one place and the registration is written once.

- `npm run build` — clean

### Not proved here

The round trip against a real api. That needs a deployment with the nonprod Supabase keys — it is the first thing to watch on QA, and the 409 path in particular has no way to be triggered by hand without two provider accounts sharing an address."""

import { CashbackApiError, type CashbackSource } from '../cashback/api';
import type { Session } from '../editorial/session';

/**
 * Who may see a cashback surface, and what happens to everybody else
 * (issue #570).
 *
 * There is no anonymous cashback surface — every route answers 401 without a
 * token, the catalogue included (FR-023). So the question each of the four
 * member pages has to answer is the same one, and it has three answers that
 * a page writing its own version will get subtly wrong:
 *
 *   * nobody is signed in — send them to sign in, and bring them back
 *   * the api refused the token they have — the same, because to a member
 *     those are one situation, and since #567 the usual cause is an account
 *     row that has not been created yet
 *   * anything else — a 503, which is the deployment's problem and not theirs
 *
 * FIXTURE MODE IS EXEMPT, and that exemption is the reason this is a module
 * rather than a one-line check. A pull-request preview has no api and nobody
 * signed in, and its entire job is to render the screens for review;
 * redirecting there would make previews useless for the one thing they are
 * for. The rule is not "is there a session" but "is there an api that would
 * refuse us".
 */

/**
 * Whether this page must send the visitor to sign in before rendering.
 *
 * `source` is the client's own answer to "am I talking to a real api", which
 * is the only honest way to ask: a page cannot tell a missing `API_BASE_URL`
 * from a preview stamp by looking at the session.
 */
export function needsSignIn(session: Session, source: CashbackSource): boolean {
  return source !== 'fixture' && !session.authenticated;
}

/**
 * Whether a failure from the cashback client was the api declining to
 * recognise the caller.
 *
 * 401 and 403 both mean it: 401 is no token or one that does not verify, 403
 * is a token that verifies for somebody this route is not for. Neither is a
 * state a member can wait out, and both are cured by signing in — which,
 * after #567, also creates the account row when it is missing.
 */
export function isUnauthorized(error: unknown): boolean {
  return error instanceof CashbackApiError && (error.status === 401 || error.status === 403);
}

import io, re

PAGES = [
  'web/src/pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/index.astro',
  'web/src/pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/[slug].astro',
  'web/src/pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/wallet.astro',
  'web/src/pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/withdraw.astro',
]

GATE = """    // FR-023: there is no anonymous cashback surface. Sending somebody to
    // sign in is the answer to that, and a 503 saying nothing is not.
    if (needsSignIn(session, api.source)) {
      return Astro.redirect(signInPath(lang, { next: here }));
    }
"""

CATCH = """} catch (error) {
  // A token the api will not accept is, to a member, the same situation as
  // no token at all - and since #567 the usual cause is an account row that
  // has not been created yet, which signing in again creates.
  if (isUnauthorized(error)) {
    return Astro.redirect(signInPath(lang, { next: here }));
  }
"""

for p in PAGES:
    s = io.open(p,'rb').read().decode('utf-8'); crlf='\r\n' in s
    b = s.replace('\r\n','\n')

    # 1. The path to come back to, declared beside the session it guards.
    m = re.search(r"^const session = sessionOf\(Astro\.request\);$", b, re.M)
    assert m, p + ": no session line"
    b = b[:m.end()] + "\n// Where signing in should bring them back to, query and all: a member\n// sent away from a filtered wallet wants that wallet back, not the top of it.\nconst here = `${Astro.url.pathname}${Astro.url.search}`;" + b[m.end():]

    # 2. The gate, immediately after the client is built.
    m = re.search(r"^(  api = createCashbackApi\(API_BASE_URL, \{\n(?:.*\n)*?  \}\);\n)", b, re.M)
    assert m, p + ": no createCashbackApi call"
    b = b[:m.end(1)] + GATE + b[m.end(1):]

    # 3. The 401 branch, first thing in the catch.
    old_catch = "} catch (error) {\n"
    i = b.index(old_catch, m.end(1))
    b = b[:i] + CATCH + b[i+len(old_catch):]

    # 4. Imports.
    anchor = "import { frontPagePath, parseAxes }"
    assert b.count(anchor) == 1, p + ": import anchor"
    b = b.replace(anchor,
        "import { signInPath } from '../../../../lib/member/access';\n"
        "import { isUnauthorized, needsSignIn } from '../../../../lib/member/gate';\n" + anchor)

    io.open(p,'wb').write((b.replace('\n','\r\n') if crlf else b).encode('utf-8'))
    print('gated', p.split('/')[-1])

import { CashbackApiError } from '../cashback/api';
import { isReadingLanguage, type ReadingLanguage } from '../reader/axes';

/**
 * Who may see a cashback surface, and what happens to everybody else
 * (issue #570).
 *
 * There is no anonymous cashback surface — every route answers 401 without a
 * token, the catalogue included (FR-023). That is a property of the whole
 * product, not of any one page, so the fence stands in the middleware beside
 * the crawler fence rather than being remembered separately by each of the
 * four member pages. A fifth page added later is gated by existing.
 *
 * FIXTURE MODE IS EXEMT FROM IT, and that exemption is the reason this is a
 * decision rather than a one-line check. A pull-request preview runs with no
 * api and nobody signed in, and its entire job is to render the screens for
 * review; redirecting there would make previews useless for the one thing
 * they exist for. So the question is not "is somebody signed in" but "is
 * there an api here that would refuse them".
 */

/** Whether this visitor must sign in before a cashback page will render. */
export function needsSignIn(authenticated: boolean, fixtures: boolean): boolean {
  return !fixtures && !authenticated;
}

/**
 * The reading language of a member cashback page, or null for anything else.
 *
 * Only `/{lang}/{place}/cashback…` is matched. `/ops` has a role of its own to
 * check and no language in its path, and `/api/cashback/…` is posted to by a
 * form — answering a POST with a redirect to a sign-in page would lose what
 * was posted, so that route keeps its own refusal.
 *
 * A language this application does not serve answers null rather than a
 * default: the page's own guard rewrites those to /404, and a fence that
 * redirected them to a Greek sign-in would be inventing a reader's language
 * on the way past (FR-009, FR-015).
 */
export function cashbackPageLanguage(pathname: string): ReadingLanguage | null {
  const match = /^\/([^/]+)\/[^/]+\/cashback(?:\/|$)/.exec(pathname);
  const lang = match?.[1];
  return lang !== undefined && isReadingLanguage(lang) ? lang : null;
}

/**
 * Whether a failure from the cashback client was the api declining to
 * recognise the caller.
 *
 * 401 and 403 both mean it: 401 is no token or one that does not verify, 403
 * is a token that verifies for somebody this route is not for.
 *
 * Note what pages must NOT do with this: redirect. Past the middleware fence
 * there IS a session, so a 401 here means the api does not recognise a person
 * who is signed in — an account row that was never created (#567), or a token
 * this deployment's JWKS will not verify. Sending them to sign in would
 * return them to the same 401 and the same redirect, forever. The page says
 * so instead, and offers the sign-in as a choice rather than taking it.
 */
export function isUnauthorized(error: unknown): boolean {
  return error instanceof CashbackApiError && (error.status === 401 || error.status === 403);
}

import { CashbackApiError, type CashbackSource } from '../cashback/api';
import type { Session } from '../editorial/session';

/**
 * Who may see a cashback surface, and what happens to everybody else
 * (issue #570).
 *
 * There is no anonymous cashback surface — every route answers 401 without a
 * token, the catalogue included (FR-023). So the question each of the four
 * member pages has to answer is the same one, and it has three answers that
 * a page writing its own version will get subtly wrong:
 *
 *   * nobody is signed in — send them to sign in, and bring them back
 *   * the api refused the token they have — the same, because to a member
 *     those are one situation, and since #567 the usual cause is an account
 *     row that has not been created yet
 *   * anything else — a 503, which is the deployment's problem and not theirs
 *
 * FIXTURE MODE IS EXEMPT, and that exemption is the reason this is a module
 * rather than a one-line check. A pull-request preview has no api and nobody
 * signed in, and its entire job is to render the screens for review;
 * redirecting there would make previews useless for the one thing they are
 * for. The rule is not "is there a session" but "is there an api that would
 * refuse us".
 */

/**
 * Whether this page must send the visitor to sign in before rendering.
 *
 * `source` is the client's own answer to "am I talking to a real api", which
 * is the only honest way to ask: a page cannot tell a missing `API_BASE_URL`
 * from a preview stamp by looking at the session.
 */
export function needsSignIn(session: Session, source: CashbackSource): boolean {
  return source !== 'fixture' && !session.authenticated;
}

/**
 * Whether a failure from the cashback client was the api declining to
 * recognise the caller.
 *
 * 401 and 403 both mean it: 401 is no token or one that does not verify, 403
 * is a token that verifies for somebody this route is not for. Neither is a
 * state a member can wait out, and both are cured by signing in — which,
 * after #567, also creates the account row when it is missing.
 */
export function isUnauthorized(error: unknown): boolean {
  return error instanceof CashbackApiError && (error.status === 401 || error.status === 403);
}

body = """Closes #570. Independent of #569 — they touch different files and either can merge first.

**FR-023: there is no anonymous cashback surface.** Every api route answers 401 without a token, the catalogue included. Until now each of the four member pages caught that 401 in the same broad `catch` that catches a dead container, so a signed-out visitor was shown:

> *nothing open in this list*

— `t.emptyQueue`, an operator's sentence about a work queue — under a **503** saying the deployment is broken. Three unrelated situations, one indistinguishable answer.

### The fence goes in the middleware

Beside the crawler fence, for the reason that one is there: this is a property of the product, not of a page, and four pages each remembering it is four chances to forget. **A fifth page is fenced by existing.**

It fences the member pages only. `/ops` has a role of its own to check and no language in its path; `/api/cashback/…` is posted to by a form, where answering with a redirect to a sign-in page would lose what was posted.

Two things it deliberately does not do:

- **Fixture mode is exempt.** A pull-request preview runs with no api and nobody signed in, and its whole job is to render the screens for review. Fencing it would make previews useless for the one thing they exist for.
- **A language this application does not serve is left alone.** The page's own guard rewrites those to `/404`; a fence that redirected them to a Greek sign-in would be inventing a reader's language on the way past (FR-009, FR-015).

The return path carries the query, because somebody sent away from a filtered wallet wants that wallet back and not the top of it.

### The 401 that survives the fence must not redirect

Past the fence there **is** a session, so a 401 from the api means it does not recognise somebody who is signed in — an account row that was never created (#567), or a token this deployment's JWKS will not verify.

Redirecting that to sign-in comes straight back, gets the same 401, and redirects again. **That is an infinite loop**, and it is the reason the pages say what happened and offer signing in again as a *choice* rather than taking it — which is also the cure, since the callback registers the account on the way through. They answer `403` while they do: the request was understood and refused, not broken.

### One decision, asked from two places

The fence needs to know whether this deployment answers from fixtures, and it is not building a client. `answersFromFixtures` is lifted out of `createCashbackApi` rather than restated, and a table-driven case pins the two together over every combination that matters. A restated copy would drift, and the way that drift would surface is a preview redirecting reviewers away from the screens they came to see.

### Copy

Every failure a member can now reach has a sentence written for a member, in `el` and `de`. The wallet's signed-out band stays, with a comment saying why: signed out is the middleware's answer now, so that band is reachable only in fixture mode — exactly the state a reviewer on a preview is in.

### A note for whoever touches frontmatter next

The first shape I wrote put the gate in each page as `if (needsSignIn(…)) return Astro.redirect(signInPath(lang, { next: here }));`. `astro check` reports `here` and the `signInPath` import as **unused**. It is not the `try`, not `Astro.redirect`, and not the condition — I tested all three. **`astro check` does not count a local whose only read is inside a frontmatter block that `return`s**, whatever the redirect mechanism. Worth knowing before somebody spends an hour on it; it also pushed this to the middleware, which is where it belonged.

- `npm run check` — 0 errors
- `npm test` — 1018 passing (55 new), coverage 95% statements / 94.4% branches / 90.4% functions
- `npm run build` — clean
- brand-literal lint — clean on a worktree with no untracked files
- `lint-refs.sh` on the branch and over the range, `lint-commit-authors.sh` over the range"""

content.text:
Both green. Here's the state.

## Merged, and confirmed on `main`

#561, #563, #565 all landed. `main` moved 23 commits from the backend side but touched nothing under `web/`, so nothing needed rebasing.

## Two new PRs, both fully green

| PR | What | Closes |
|---|---|---|
| [#569](https://github.com/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/pull/569) | **Signing in makes the member an account** | #567 |
| [#573](https://github.com/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/pull/573) | **A cashback page without a member sends them to sign in** | #570 |

They're independent — either order, no conflicts.

**#569** closes the gap #565 left open. A session isn't an account: every cashback route looks the caller up in `account` and 401s when there's no row, so a member who signed in successfully found the wallet, catalogue and click-out all failing while nothing *looked* broken. `/auth/confirm` now calls `POST /api/v1/account` (your #544) straight after the exchange. The interesting part is the refusals: a 409 (address already another account's) drops the session and says what to try instead, because a session that reaches nothing is worse than none; an unreachable api lands with the *successes*, because a preview has none at all.

**#573** puts the sign-in fence in the middleware rather than in four pages — same reasoning as the crawler fence already there, and a fifth page gets fenced by existing. Previews stay exempt, or they'd redirect reviewers away from the screens they exist to show.

One thing worth flagging from #573: the obvious shape — `if (needsSignIn(…)) return Astro.redirect(signInPath(…))` in each page — makes `astro check` report the locals as **unused**. I tested it three ways: it's not the `try`, not `Astro.redirect`, not the condition. `astro check` doesn't count a local whose only read sits inside a frontmatter block that `return`s. It's in the PR body so the next person doesn't lose an hour to it. It also pushed the fence to the middleware, which is where it belonged.

I also found and avoided a real trap: redirecting on a 401 *past* the fence is an infinite loop, since the member does have a session. Those pages state the situation and offer sign-in as a choice.

## What's next

F3, with your answer: I'll write `/{lang}/terms` as a plain-language statement of what the code actually enforces — rate snapshotted at click, pending until the shop confirms, reversed on a refund, paid only to a destination proved yours above the threshold, leaving keeps the records. Each line traceable to a mechanism, no invented obligations. Then the opt-in screen posting `brand.legal.documents.terms.version`, which is the exact field `Participations.Join` compares.

After that: F1.4 (the flag-gated shell exchange, which unblocks the browser test), then F4/F5/F6 verification against the now-live catalogue endpoint.

One housekeeping note: `main` now tracks `.mcp.json` with the IcePanel server, which displaced my local one configuring graft. I backed the local copy up rather than lose it. If you want both, that's a one-line addition to the tracked file — say the word and I'll fold it into a chore commit.

# Housekeeping, then F3 · F1.4 · F4–F6

## Context

Five PRs have merged (#561, #563, #565, #569 pending, #573 pending) and the
backend closed B1, B2, B4 and B5. Two of the founder's own housekeeping items
now come first, then the remaining frontend work on the path to one real
transaction.

The founder asked for, in priority order:

1. **`.mcp.json` carries both servers.** `main` now tracks it with IcePanel
   only, which displaced a local file configuring graft. Both are wanted.
2. **Close the stale issues.** Many were implemented but never referenced by a
   PR, so nothing auto-closed them.
3. **F3** — opt-in and the terms route, on my own judgement (settled: I draft
   the terms as a statement of what the code enforces, each line traceable).
4. **F1.4 and F4/F5/F6** — planned and executed.

*(F1.4 and F4–F6 sections pending exploration results.)*

---

## 1 — `.mcp.json`: both servers *(one small PR, first)*

`main` tracks:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "icepanel": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.icepanel.io/mcp" } } }
```

The displaced local file configured graft as a stdio server
(`npx -y @nanonets/graft mcp`). Both belong in the tracked file — graft is
already a first-class part of how this repo is navigated (there is a
`.claude/skills/graft/` and a SessionStart hook that points at it).

**One thing that goes stale with it**, and it is the reason this is a PR and
not a one-line edit: `docs/architecture/icepanel-model.md:2030` says the file
*"names a server and nothing else"*, and
`docs/architecture/README.md:85` points at it. The sentence stops being true
the moment a second server is added, so it changes in the same commit.

Nothing validates `.mcp.json` — no script, workflow or Makefile target reads
it — so there is no check to extend.

---

## 2 — Stale issues: close what the tree proves is built

The founder's read is right, and the evidence is entirely local — which
matters, because **GitHub's secondary rate limit is currently refusing this
account's content requests**, and any plan that needs one API call per issue
will stall. The method below needs two or three reads and one write per issue
actually closed.

### The evidence, gathered without the API

Three independent signals, all computable from the tree:

| Signal | How | Found |
|---|---|---|
| A commit on `main` names the issue | `git log --format=%s` → `(#N)` | **173 distinct numbers** |
| Code or config cites the issue | `git grep '#NNN'` over `internal/ web/src/ cmd/ scripts/ deploy/` | **83 numbers** |
| The artifact the issue names exists | issue title names a file/symbol; check the tree | per issue |

**By hand, from section 2 and section 3.** The tables are ordered so that a parent always appears before its children within a domain, and the domains are ordered Platform, Cashback, News, Delivery for the same reason. Create the four domains, then the objects top-down, then the connections. The source path is a link in every row, so a modeller can open the code beside the box.

# Housekeeping, then F3 · F1.4 · F4–F6

## Context

Five PRs have merged (#561, #563, #565, #569 pending, #573 pending) and the
backend closed B1, B2, B4 and B5. Two of the founder's own housekeeping items
now come first, then the remaining frontend work on the path to one real
transaction.

The founder asked for, in priority order:

1. **`.mcp.json` carries both servers.** `main` now tracks it with IcePanel
   only, which displaced a local file configuring graft. Both are wanted.
2. **Close the stale issues.** Many were implemented but never referenced by a
   PR, so nothing auto-closed them.
3. **F3** — opt-in and the terms route, on my own judgement (settled: I draft
   the terms as a statement of what the code enforces, each line traceable).
4. **F1.4 and F4/F5/F6** — planned and executed.

*(F1.4 and F4–F6 sections pending exploration results.)*

---

## 1 — `.mcp.json`: both servers *(one small PR, first)*

`main` tracks:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "icepanel": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.icepanel.io/mcp" } } }
```

The displaced local file configured graft as a stdio server
(`npx -y @nanonets/graft mcp`). Both belong in the tracked file — graft is
already a first-class part of how this repo is navigated (there is a
`.claude/skills/graft/` and a SessionStart hook that points at it).

**One thing that goes stale with it**, and it is the reason this is a PR and
not a one-line edit: `docs/architecture/icepanel-model.md:2030` says the file
*"names a server and nothing else"*, and
`docs/architecture/README.md:85` points at it. The sentence stops being true
the moment a second server is added, so it changes in the same commit.

Nothing validates `.mcp.json` — no script, workflow or Makefile target reads
it — so there is no check to extend.

---

## 2 — Stale issues: close what the tree proves is built

The founder's read is right, and the evidence is entirely local — which
matters, because **GitHub's secondary rate limit is currently refusing this
account's content requests**, and any plan that needs one API call per issue
will stall. The method below needs two or three reads and one write per issue
actually closed.

### The evidence, gathered without the API

Three independent signals, all computable from the tree:

| Signal | How | Found |
|---|---|---|
| A commit on `main` names the issue | `git log --format=%s` → `(#N)` | **173 distinct numbers** |
| Code or config cites the issue | `git grep '#NNN'` over `internal/ web/src/ cmd/ scripts/ deploy/` | **83 numbers** |
| The artifact the issue names exists | issue title names a file/symbol; check the tree | per issue |

Union of the first two: **197 issue numbers with implementation evidence.**
Intersecting that with the open-issue list is the candidate set.

### Why the obvious source is not usable

`specs/*/tasks.md` checkboxes look authoritative and are not.
`specs/002-apivo-cashback-alpha/tasks.md` reports 81 done / 66 open, yet
T001–T006 are all unchecked and all plainly built — the cashback config keys,
the `blnk`/`redis` compose services, the `cashback` CI job. The checkboxes
have the same drift the issues do. **Evidence comes from code and history,
never from a checkbox.**

### How each issue is judged

- **Tier A — close.** A commit subject on `main` carries `(#N)`. That is the
  repository's own convention for "this commit did that", and an issue still
  open under one was simply never referenced by a PR body. Closed with a
  comment citing the commits.
- **Tier B — verify, then close or leave.** No commit reference, but the title
  names a concrete artifact (`internal/cashback/payout/handlers.go`, a route,
  a symbol). Check the artifact and its tests. `#242` is the shape of this:
  no commit cites it, and every handler it asks for exists.
- **Tier C — leave open, and list.** Anything ambiguous, anything for an
  unbuilt feature (the `003-cashback-claims` backlog, #448–#492, is not
  built), and anything where the artifact exists but the issue asks for more
  than the artifact.

Tier C is reported to the founder rather than guessed at. A wrongly closed
issue is a task that quietly stops existing.

### Rate-limit discipline

Two or three reads to list the open issues, then all judgement is local. Each
close is one `PATCH` (`state: closed`, `state_reason: completed`) plus one
comment. Batched with pauses and resumable from a written work-list, so a
secondary limit part-way through costs nothing but time.

*(remaining sections pending)*

=== what it does ===
feat(clickout): the click-out refuses a member who has not opted in (#568)

FR-110. Nothing checked it: a signed-in member who never accepted the
terms could click out, be redirected and later be credited, and FR-002's
opt-in is not one if a credit can precede it.

The service takes an Enrolment - is this member in cashback right now -
as a required part, not an option, because the whole finding was that a
root could leave the check out. The wallet's participation service
satisfies it directly. The read comes after the click rule and before the
catalogue: a member who cannot click is refused before anything is read,
minted or recorded, and a read that failed is a failure rather than a
refusal. The handler answers 403 - the member is who they say they are;
what is missing is a consent - and names where to give it.

api/openapi.json declares the 403; the contract test reaches it. The
journeys and the scenario harness opt their members in before clicking,
as members would have, and the wiring test walks both gates.

# 1. `GET /api/v1/cashback/catalogue`

**Files:** `C:\Users\madym\repos\apivo-news\internal\cashback\catalogue\list.go`, `...\list_handlers.go`, `...\handlers.go`

### Query parameters (names at `handlers.go:49-60`)

```go
const (
	placeParam    = "place"
	searchParam   = "q"
	limitParam    = "limit"
	cursorParam   = "cursor"
	categoryParam = "category"
)
const languageParam = "lang"
```

| Param | Required | Validation | Failure |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lang` | **yes** | `normaliseLanguage` = `strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(tag))` (`copy.go:142-144`), then `languageSubtag = ^[a-z]{2,3}$` (`list.go:75`) | 400 `"lang is required: the reader's language as a BCP-47 primary subtag, such as el or de"` |
| `place` | **yes**, repeatable | `query[placeParam]` → `distinctSlugs` trims/drops-empty/de-dupes (`list.go:293-305`); each must resolve in `PlacesBySlugs` | none → 400 `"place is required: …"`; unknown → 400 `"no such place: \"xyz\""` (`list_handlers.go:74-78`) |
| `q` | no | see below | never fails |
| `limit` | no | `strconv.Atoi`; `err != nil \|\| n < 1` → 400 (`list_handlers.go:51-58`) | 400 `"limit must be a positive whole number"` |
| `cursor` | no | `decodeListCursor` | 400 `"cursor is not one this listing issued; start again without it"` |
| `category` | **refused if present at all** | `if query.Has(categoryParam)` | 400 `"category has nothing behind it yet and is refused rather than ignored (#414)"` |

Note: unknown/extra query parameters are **not** rejected here (unlike `/wallet/entries`, §6).

Also note `ErrCategoryUnbuilt` (`list.go:68`) is declared and never used — the handler inlines the 400. Dead symbol, harmless.

### Response envelope (`list_handlers.go:24-41`)

```go
type catalogueItemResponse struct {
	MerchantID     string         `json:"merchant_id"`
	Slug           string         `json:"slug"`
	Name           string         `json:"name"`
	NameLanguage   string         `json:"name_language"`
	NameIsFallback bool           `json:"name_is_fallback"`
	Summary        *string        `json:"summary"`
	Rates          []rateResponse `json:"rates"`
}

type cataloguePageResponse struct {
	Items []catalogueItemResponse `json:"items"`
	NextCursor *string `json:"next_cursor"`
}
```

`Items` is always a list (never null); `next_cursor` is `null` on the last page (`list_handlers.go:109-112`). Status 200.

### Cursor and limit

Constants at `list.go:30-48`:

```go
	DefaultListLimit = 20
	MaxListLimit = 100
	listCursorTag = "catalogue"
	listCursorSeparator = "|"
	maxListCursorBytes = 256
```

- **Cursor content:** `base64.RawURLEncoding` of `"catalogue|<merchant slug>"` (`list.go:310-312`). It is a **keyset on the slug**, in Go byte order, deliberately sorted in Go rather than by SQL (`list.go:136-141`).
- **Max limit:** 100, **capped, not refused** (`list.go:157-162`): `case limit > MaxListLimit: limit = MaxListLimit`. Zero/absent → 20.
- **Invalid cursor:** `ErrBadCursor` → **400**. Rejected for: `len(raw) > 256`, non-base64url, no `|`, wrong tag, or empty slug (`list.go:316-332`). Empty string is the first page, not an error.
- **How next_cursor is produced** (`list.go:198-218`): reads `limit+1` items, then

```go
	if len(items) > limit {
		page.Items = items[:limit]
		page.NextCursor = encodeListCursor(items[limit-1].Slug)
	}
```

### What it does with `q` (`list.go:196`, `206-208`)

```go
	search := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(q.Search))
	…
	if search != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(described.Name), search) {
		continue
	}
```

Substring, case-folded via `strings.ToLower`, **against the resolved display name only** — not the summary, not the slug. Blank/whitespace `q` means "everything". Worth knowing for F4: `strings.ToLower` is not accent-folding, so Greek `ΑΓΟΡΆ` → `αγορά` ≠ `αγορα`; accent-insensitive search does not work.

### Compared with `web/src/lib/cashback/api.ts` `catalogue()` (lines 344-358)

```ts
    catalogue: (query) => {
      const search = new URLSearchParams();
      search.set('lang', query.lang);
      for (const place of query.places) {
        search.append('place', place);
      }
      if (query.q !== undefined && query.q !== '') {
        search.set('q', query.q);
      }
      search.set('limit', String(query.limit ?? DEFAULT_LIMIT));
      if (query.cursor !== undefined) {
        search.set('cursor', query.cursor);
      }
      return required<OperatorPage<CatalogueItem>>(`/catalogue?${search.toString()}`);
    },
```

**Mismatches / gaps:**

1. **No wire-shape mismatch.** `CatalogueItem` (`web/src/lib/cashback/types.ts:59-73`) matches `catalogueItemResponse` field for field, and `OperatorPage<T>` (`types.ts:298-301`) matches the envelope (`items`, `next_cursor: string | null`).
2. **`limit` is always sent** (`DEFAULT_LIMIT = 20`, `api.ts:166`). It is never omitted, so the server's own default never applies and the shelf is hard-capped at 20 unless a caller passes `limit`. No caller does.
3. **`cursor` is plumbed in the client but no caller supplies it.** `CatalogueQuery.cursor` (`api.ts:98`) exists; `index.astro` never sets it.
4. **The fixture client cannot paginate at all.** `api.ts:193-202` ignores `query.cursor` entirely and `page()` (`api.ts:170-172`) hard-codes `next_cursor: null`. Any "next page" UI you build for F4 will be dead in dev/preview until the fixture is taught to slice by cursor.
5. **No client-side handling of the 400s.** `q` OK, but an unknown `place` slug is a 400 from the server, and `index.astro` funnels every non-401/403 into the 503 "page unavailable" band (see §2). A reader place axis with no `cashback` place row takes the whole catalogue page down with `Retry-After: 60`.
6. `category` is never sent by the client — correct, since sending it is an unconditional 400.
7. Minor: `search.set('cursor', '')` is possible if a caller passes `cursor: ''`; server reads it as first page, so it is safe but sloppy.

**Path:** `C:\Users\madym\repos\apivo-news\web\src\pages\[lang]\[place]\cashback\index.astro` (369 lines)

**It throws it away.** Line 70:

```ts

```

No `limit`, no `cursor`, and `.items` destructured off the page. `next_cursor` is never bound to a variable anywhere on the page.

### Pagination UI

**None.** There is no "next", no page links, no load-more, no `cursor` in any URL. The only URL state is `q` (line 53).

Downstream consequence: the counter at line 96

```ts
const aside = t.partnersCount(items.length, placeNames);
```

reports **at most 20**, and the empty state at line 149 (`items.length === 0`) is the only "there is more/less" signal on the page. This is the same class of bug as `allCount` in the wallet (§5).

### States it renders

| State | Line | Rendering |

| fixture mode | 114 | `<FixtureNotice title={t.cashback} body={t.fixtureNotice} />` |
| `unrecognised` (401/403 from api, status 403) | 142-147 | `t.notRecognised` + sign-in link |

**Defined and never used, anywhere in the codebase.**

- Declared: `web/src/i18n/cashback.ts:74` — `readonly placementNotForSale: string;`
- Greek value: `cashback.ts:323`; German value: `cashback.ts:566`; and per-language equivalents.


and the explainer `t.shelfP1` (`cashback.ts:699`) repeats it at length. So the disclosure *is* on the page; the dedicated string for it is orphaned.

Counted by grepping `t.<key>` across all of `web/src` excluding `src/i18n/`:

# 3. Click-out

### The form (`[slug].astro:217-233`)

```astro
              {
                firstRate !== undefined ? (
                  <form method="post" action="/api/cashback/clickout">
                    <input type="hidden" name="offer_id" value={firstRate.offer_id} />
                    <input type="hidden" name="back" value={backHere} />
                    <button class="btn btn-primary btn-block shop" type="submit">
                      {t.shopAtTracking(merchant.name)}
                    </button>
                    <div class="opens">{t.opensTracked}</div>
                  </form>

                  <p class="no-rates">{t.noRatesToday}</p>
                )
              }
```

Plain `multipart/form-data` POST, no JS. `backHere = merchantPath(lang, slugs, slug)` (line 98).

### Only `rates[0]` is offered — confirmed

`[slug].astro:105`:

```ts
const firstRate = merchant?.rates[0];
```

The rate **table** (lines 170-183) renders every band with its `valid_to`, conditions and exclusions, but **only band 0 has a click-out button**. If a merchant publishes two bands, a member cannot click through on the second at all. `rateResponse.offer_id` exists per band, so the API already supports it — this is purely a UI omission and is the biggest F5 item.

### What `?clickout=<status>` does today

`[slug].astro:97`:

```ts
const clickoutFailed = Astro.url.searchParams.has('clickout');
```

**Read with `.has()`, value discarded** — you are right. Rendered at line 133:

```astro
    {clickoutFailed && <p class="band" role="alert">{t.clickoutFailed}</p>}
```

So all six distinct API failures collapse into one sentence.

### Copy that exists for failures

Only **one** string: `t.clickoutFailed`, declared `web/src/i18n/cashback.ts:85`, with values at `:337` (el) / `:579` (de) etc. There is **no** per-status copy — nothing for 429/rate-limited, nothing for 409/expired, nothing for 502/no-redirect, nothing for 401. `t.noRatesToday` (`:77`) covers the no-band case, and `t.pageUnavailable`/`t.notRecognised` cover the *page* load, not the click-out. Writing 4-6 new strings is an F5 deliverable.

### `web/src/pages/api/cashback/clickout.ts` — full behaviour

| Path | Line | Response |
|---|---|---|
| cross-origin | 26-28 | **plain-text 403** `'cross-origin click-out refused'` — no redirect, bare text page |
| missing/blank `offer_id` | 33-35 | **plain-text 400** `'offer_id is required'` — same |
| `createCashbackApi` throws | 38-42 | **outside the `try`** → unhandled → Astro 500. In `APP_ENV=prod` with no `API_BASE_URL` this is a raw error page, not a redirect back. |
| success | 45-46 | `redirect(redirect_url, 303)` |
| any API error | 47-54 | `redirect(\`${target}?clickout=${status}\`, 303)` |

```ts
    const status = error instanceof CashbackApiError ? error.status : 502;
    const target = typeof back === 'string' && back.startsWith('/') ? back : '/';
    return redirect(`${target}?clickout=${status}`, 303);
```

Two defects to fix in F5:

1. **`back.startsWith('/')` admits `//evil.com`** — a protocol-relative URL, i.e. an open redirect on the failure path. The repo already has the correct helper: `safeReturnPath` in `web/src/lib/member/access.ts` explicitly rejects it — `if (!raw.startsWith('/') || raw.startsWith('//')) return fallback;`. Use it.
2. **`?` is appended unconditionally.** Today `back` is always `merchantPath(...)` with no query, so it works; the moment `back` carries one it produces `/el/munich/cashback/x?a=1?clickout=409`.

`internal\cashback\clickout\handlers.go` and `...\auth.go`:

| Status | Where | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **401** | `auth.go:57` | `"a bearer token is required"` — no `Authorization` header. Sets `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="cashback"`. |
| **401** | `auth.go:64` | `"the bearer token is invalid or belongs to no account"` — `ErrUnauthenticated`. Sets `error="invalid_token"`. |
| **500** | `auth.go:68` | Authentication itself failed (DB/JWKS outage). |
| **400** | `handlers.go:215` | Body is not valid JSON for this endpoint (`DisallowUnknownFields`). |
| **400** | `handlers.go:223` | More than one JSON document in the body. |

```ts
export async function allSources(api: EditorialApi, maxPages = 10): Promise<SourceList> {
  const first = await api.sources();
  const items: SourceRow[] = [...first.items];
  let cursor = first.next_cursor ?? null;
  let pages = 1;
  while (cursor !== null && pages < maxPages) {

    items.push(...page.items);
    cursor = page.next_cursor ?? null;
```

```ts
export async function allSources(api: EditorialApi, maxPages = 10): Promise<SourceList> {
  const first = await api.sources();
  const items: SourceRow[] = [...first.items];
  let cursor = first.next_cursor ?? null;
  let pages = 1;
  while (cursor !== null && pages < maxPages) {
    const page = await api.sources(cursor);
    items.push(...page.items);
    cursor = page.next_cursor ?? null;
    pages += 1;
  }
  return { items, cycle: first.cycle, fixture: first.fixture === true, truncated: cursor !== null };
}
```

- **How next_cursor is produced** (`list.go:198-218`): reads `limit+1` items, then

```go
	if len(items) > limit {

		page.NextCursor = encodeListCursor(items[limit-1].Slug)
	}
```

```ts
export async function allSources(api: EditorialApi, maxPages = 10): Promise<SourceList> {
  const first = await api.sources();
  const items: SourceRow[] = [...first.items];
  let cursor = first.next_cursor ?? null;
  let pages = 1;
  while (cursor !== null && pages < maxPages) {
    const page = await api.sources(cursor);
    items.push(...page.items);
    cursor = page.next_cursor ?? null;
    pages += 1;
  }
  return { items, cycle: first.cycle, fixture: first.fixture === true, truncated: cursor !== null };
}
```

It also models the **`truncated` flag** — `SourceList.truncated` (`api.ts:895-908`) — "the bound was hit with a cursor still on offer, say so rather than presenting the count as the whole registry." That is exactly the honesty property `allCount` needs, and `sources.astro:228` is the precedent for wiring it into a page. Lift the shape (a `SourceList`-like `{items, truncated}`) rather than the function.

So: for F4/F6 you are inventing the *first* real "next page" UI in this codebase. There is no component to reuse — only the exhaust-and-flag helper.

```go
// mint signs an RS256 token for one subject. The claims are the ones the
// verifier actually checks - sub, iat, exp - and nothing more: a token
// carrying claims this deployment ignores would suggest they mattered.
func mint(key jwk.Key, subject uuid.UUID) (string, error) {
	now := time.Now()
	token, err := jwt.NewBuilder().
		Subject(subject.String()).
		IssuedAt(now.Add(-time.Minute)).
		Expiration(now.Add(tokenLifetime)).
		Build()
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	signed, err := jwt.Sign(token, jwt.WithKey(jwa.RS256(), key))
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return string(signed), nil
}
```

```ts
export const FORWARDED_PROTO_HEADER = 'x-forwarded-proto';

export function forwardedProto(raw: string | null | undefined): string | null {
  if (raw === null || raw === undefined) {
    return null;
  }
  const first = raw.split(',')[0]?.trim().toLowerCase() ?? '';
  return first === '' ? null : first;
}

export function isSecureRequest(request: Request, appEnv: string | undefined | null): boolean {
  if (isProdEnv(appEnv)) {
    return true;
  }
  const forwarded = forwardedProto(request.headers.get(FORWARDED_PROTO_HEADER));
  if (forwarded !== null) {
    return forwarded === 'https';
  }
  return new URL(request.url).protocol === 'https:';
}
```

## 7. CSRF / signed cookies / HMAC — definitive answer

**There is a CSRF module, but it holds no token. There is no signed cookie, no HMAC helper, and no crypto of any kind in `web/`.**

`web/src/lib/csrf.ts` exports exactly one function plus a private helper:

```ts
export function isSameOrigin(request: Request, siteOrigin: string): boolean
```

It compares the **host** of `Origin` (falling back to `Referer`) against the host of the site origin; a request with neither is refused. Host, not full origin, because `@astrojs/node` builds `Astro.url` from the socket (lines 26-51 explain at length). Its own docblock, lines 13-15, states the gap you are looking at:

```
 * The check goes in before real approvals exist rather than after, so
 * enabling auth cannot silently open the hole. It is a floor, not a
 * ceiling: a per-session token belongs here too once there are sessions
 * to bind one to.
```

Nine call sites: `pages/ops/{withdrawals,reconciliation,unattributed,held}.astro:14`, `pages/api/cashback/clickout.ts:5`, `pages/[lang]/signin.astro:7`, `pages/[lang]/editor/{audit,index,signin,sources}.astro`, `pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/withdraw.astro:26`. Usage pattern (`signin.astro:72-74`):

```ts
  if (!isSameOrigin(Astro.request, Astro.url.origin)) {
    return new Response('cross-origin sign-in refused', { status: 403 });
  }
```

**Absent, verified by grep across `web/src`:** `node:crypto`, `createHmac`, `timingSafeEqual`, `crypto.subtle`, `randomUUID`, `jose`, `jsonwebtoken`, `jwtVerify`. `web/package.json` dependencies are only `@astrojs/node`, `@supabase/ssr`, `astro`, `driver.js`.

**Implication for F1.4:** you have no signing primitive. Two honest options: (a) store the bearer token in the cookie verbatim, `httpOnly`, and let *the API* remain the only verifier — the cookie is a bearer credential, not an assertion, so it needs no signature of ours; (b) pull in `jose` to verify against `JWKS_URL` on the web side too, which duplicates a check the API already does. (a) matches the existing design (`resolveSession` never trusts cookie contents either — it round-trips to the auth server). If you go with (a), your exchange route must verify the token *once*, at exchange time, by calling the API (`GET /api/v1/account` with the bearer) and only minting the cookie on a 2xx — that is "confirms it" without any crypto in `web/`. Node 22 is the floor (`engines`), so `node:crypto` is available if you later need it.

## 4 — F5: click-out, end to end *(two PRs, and one of them is a fix)*

The edge half is **done and proven**: `snippets.caddy:96` is now
`@api path /api/v1/* /healthz /readyz`, and `deploy/hetzner/validate.sh:646,658`
asserts both halves — api routes to the api, `/api/cashback/clickout` and
`/api/tour/*` to the web, previews included.

### 4a — the click-out endpoint's own defects *(fix first)*

`web/src/pages/api/cashback/clickout.ts` has three, found while surveying:

1. **An open redirect on the failure path.** `back.startsWith('/')` admits
   `//evil.example`, which is protocol-relative and leaves the site. This
   repository already owns the correct check — `safeReturnPath`
   (`web/src/lib/member/access.ts`), written for exactly this in #564, which
   rejects it explicitly. Use it.
2. **`createCashbackApi` sits outside the `try`.** In `APP_ENV=prod` with no
   `API_BASE_URL` it throws a raw Astro 500 at a member mid-click instead of
   redirecting back with a status.
3. **`?` is appended unconditionally**, so the moment `back` carries a query
   it builds `…?a=1?clickout=409`.

### 4b — the click-out a member can act on

Today `[slug].astro:97` reads the outcome with `.has()` and throws the value
away, so six distinct API answers collapse into one sentence
(`t.clickoutFailed`). The Go handler distinguishes them, and each wants a
different move from the member:

| Status | Means | What the page should say |
|---|---|---|
| **403** | **not opted in** — B3/#568 landed this while I was working | point at the opt-in screen; this is the one that is *actionable* |
| 429 | the click rule, with `Retry-After` | wait, and say roughly how long |
| 409 | band expired or retailer inactive | the offer is gone; the page reloads to show what is left |
| 502 | no deeplink could be built; **nothing was recorded** | try again, safely |
| 401 | no session | the fence handles it; belt and braces |
| 400 | a bad offer id | our fault, not theirs |

The 429's `Retry-After` is currently dropped by the web endpoint — only the
number `429` survives into the query string.

**Every published band gets a button.** `[slug].astro:105` takes
`merchant?.rates[0]` and only that one, so a retailer publishing two bands has
one a member cannot click at all. The rate table already renders them all and
each carries its own `offer_id`.

## 5 — F4: the catalogue on the real endpoint *(one PR)*

The endpoint is complete and its shape already matches `types.ts` field for
field. What is missing is on this side:

- **`next_cursor` is discarded** (`index.astro:70`) and there is no paging UI
  anywhere in this codebase to copy. The shelf is hard-capped at 20 because
  the client always sends `limit`, so the server's own default never applies.
- **`t.partnersCount(items.length, …)` presents 20 as the total.** The
  honest shape already exists: `allSources`
  (`web/src/lib/editorial/api.ts:911-940`) follows a cursor to a bound and
  returns a `truncated` flag, with `sources.astro` as the precedent for
  rendering it. Lift the shape, not the function.
- **The fixture client cannot paginate** (`api.ts:193-202` ignores `cursor`,
  `page()` hard-codes `next_cursor: null`), so any control built here is dead
  in dev and on previews until the fixture honours a cursor.
- **An unknown place slug is a 400** and currently takes the whole page down
  as a 503 with `Retry-After: 60`.
- `t.placementNotForSale` is defined in both languages and rendered nowhere;
  `t.sortedNote` carries the claim instead. Use one and delete the other —
  along with `noteColumn`, `confirmationTimeUnknown`, `merchantNotFound`,
  `reservedExplained` and `payoutThreshold`, all defined and never rendered.

## 6 — F6: the wallet against real entries *(one PR)*

Three defects, one of them a correctness bug rather than a cosmetic one:

- **`?entry=<id>` silently resolves against page one.** `explicit` searches
  only the 20 loaded entries, so a member linked to their 21st entry is shown
  their 1st. That is the one to fix first.
- **`allCount` is `min(total, 20)`** (`wallet.astro:101` calls `api.entries()`
  unfiltered and takes `.items.length`), so the count reads "20 of 20"
  forever. It also doubles the wallet's API traffic on every render.
- **`lang` is never sent on `entries()`**, so `merchant_name_is_fallback` is
  true for every row and the wallet prints "shown in <language>" on all of
  them. A one-line addition to `EntryQuery`.

`GET /wallet/entries` is already cursor-complete server-side and needs no Go
change.

*(F1.4 pending the second exploration result)*

# Housekeeping, then F3 · F1.4 · F4–F6

## Context

Five PRs have merged (#561, #563, #565, #569 pending, #573 pending) and the
backend closed B1, B2, B4 and B5. Two of the founder's own housekeeping items
now come first, then the remaining frontend work on the path to one real
transaction.

The founder asked for, in priority order:

1. **`.mcp.json` carries both servers.** `main` now tracks it with IcePanel
   only, which displaced a local file configuring graft. Both are wanted.
2. **Close the stale issues.** Many were implemented but never referenced by a
   PR, so nothing auto-closed them.
3. **F3** — opt-in and the terms route, on my own judgement (settled: I draft
   the terms as a statement of what the code enforces, each line traceable).
4. **F1.4 and F4/F5/F6** — planned and executed.

*(F1.4 and F4–F6 sections pending exploration results.)*

---

## 1 — `.mcp.json`: both servers *(one small PR, first)*

`main` tracks:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "icepanel": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.icepanel.io/mcp" } } }
```

The displaced local file configured graft as a stdio server
(`npx -y @nanonets/graft mcp`). Both belong in the tracked file — graft is
already a first-class part of how this repo is navigated (there is a
`.claude/skills/graft/` and a SessionStart hook that points at it).

**One thing that goes stale with it**, and it is the reason this is a PR and
not a one-line edit: `docs/architecture/icepanel-model.md:2030` says the file
*"names a server and nothing else"*, and
`docs/architecture/README.md:85` points at it. The sentence stops being true
the moment a second server is added, so it changes in the same commit.

Nothing validates `.mcp.json` — no script, workflow or Makefile target reads
it — so there is no check to extend.

---

## 2 — Stale issues: close what the tree proves is built

The founder's read is right, and the evidence is entirely local — which
matters, because **GitHub's secondary rate limit is currently refusing this
account's content requests**, and any plan that needs one API call per issue
will stall. The method below needs two or three reads and one write per issue
actually closed.

### The evidence, gathered without the API

Three independent signals, all computable from the tree:

| Signal | How | Found |
|---|---|---|
| A commit on `main` names the issue | `git log --format=%s` → `(#N)` | **173 distinct numbers** |
| Code or config cites the issue | `git grep '#NNN'` over `internal/ web/src/ cmd/ scripts/ deploy/` | **83 numbers** |
| The artifact the issue names exists | issue title names a file/symbol; check the tree | per issue |

Union of the first two: **197 issue numbers with implementation evidence.**
Intersecting that with the open-issue list is the candidate set.

### Why the obvious source is not usable

`specs/*/tasks.md` checkboxes look authoritative and are not.
`specs/002-apivo-cashback-alpha/tasks.md` reports 81 done / 66 open, yet
T001–T006 are all unchecked and all plainly built — the cashback config keys,
the `blnk`/`redis` compose services, the `cashback` CI job. The checkboxes
have the same drift the issues do. **Evidence comes from code and history,
never from a checkbox.**

### How each issue is judged

- **Tier A — close.** A commit subject on `main` carries `(#N)`. That is the
  repository's own convention for "this commit did that", and an issue still
  open under one was simply never referenced by a PR body. Closed with a
  comment citing the commits.
- **Tier B — verify, then close or leave.** No commit reference, but the title
  names a concrete artifact (`internal/cashback/payout/handlers.go`, a route,
  a symbol). Check the artifact and its tests. `#242` is the shape of this:
  no commit cites it, and every handler it asks for exists.
- **Tier C — leave open, and list.** Anything ambiguous, anything for an
  unbuilt feature (the `003-cashback-claims` backlog, #448–#492, is not
  built), and anything where the artifact exists but the issue asks for more
  than the artifact.

Tier C is reported to the founder rather than guessed at. A wrongly closed
issue is a task that quietly stops existing.

### Rate-limit discipline

Two or three reads to list the open issues, then all judgement is local. Each
close is one `PATCH` (`state: closed`, `state_reason: completed`) plus one
comment. Batched with pauses and resumable from a written work-list, so a
secondary limit part-way through costs nothing but time.

---

## 3 — F3: the terms, and the opt-in *(two PRs)*

### 3a — `/{lang}/terms`

Its own route in the legal family — same layout, masthead and language
switcher as `/{lang}/impressum` — but **not** a fourth `LegalPane`.
`LegalPane` renders term/value pairs out of `brand.legal` (entity, address,
jurisdiction); the cashback terms are prose, and forcing them through it would
distort a component that currently does one thing well.

Content lives in a new `web/src/lib/legal/terms.ts` beside
`lib/legal/strings.ts`, in `el` and `de`, with the version rendered from
`brand.legal.documents.terms.version` — the same field
`Participations.Join` compares (`internal/cashback/wallet/participations.go:162`).

Each clause states a rule the code actually enforces, and nothing else:

| Clause | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| the rate shown when you clicked is the rate that applies | FR-013, the band snapshotted onto the click |
| an entry is pending until the shop confirms it | `earnings/state.go` — `held pending confirmed reserved paid reversed` |
| a refund reverses it, and both rows stay visible | `reversal_of_id`, US3 scenario 2 |
| money is paid only to an account proved yours | FR-051, `verified_at` |
| there is a floor before a payout | `payout_threshold` |
| leaving stops the earning and keeps the records | FR-003 — a status and a date, never a deletion |
| balances are a claim on a future rebate | founder decision Q2, ADR-0002 |

No invented obligations, no boilerplate, and the PR says plainly that
counsel-approved text replaces this before launch.

**Not** linked from the site footer. That carries the three notices a
German-facing service legally owes; these are product terms, reached from the
opt-in screen and from the wallet.

### 3b — the opt-in screen

Reached when `GET /participation` answers 404 — which is not an error, and the
contract says so. Posts `brand.legal.documents.terms.version`; a 400 means the
version moved under the member and the page reloads rather than re-posting a
stale consent; a 503 means the deployment names no brand (`ErrNoBrand`) and
the page says so rather than retrying.

The wallet's not-participating band stops pointing at the catalogue and points
here. `api.optIn()` has existed with zero call sites since it was written.

### Branch order

F3 touches `wallet.astro` and `i18n/cashback.ts`, both of which #573 also
touches, and F1.4 touches `middleware.ts`, which #573 changes as well. So each
branches from `main` once #569 and #573 have merged, and stacks on them with
`gh stack` if they have not. Verified before branching, not assumed.

*(F1.4 and F4–F6 pending exploration results)*

```go
func mint(key jwk.Key, subject uuid.UUID) (string, error) {
	now := time.Now()
	token, err := jwt.NewBuilder().
		Subject(subject.String()).
		IssuedAt(now.Add(-time.Minute)).
		Expiration(now.Add(tokenLifetime)).

	}

	}

}
```

```ts
export const FORWARDED_PROTO_HEADER = 'x-forwarded-proto';

export function forwardedProto(raw: string | null | undefined): string | null {
  if (raw === null || raw === undefined) {
    return null;
  }
  const first = raw.split(',')[0]?.trim().toLowerCase() ?? '';
  return first === '' ? null : first;
}

export function isSecureRequest(request: Request, appEnv: string | undefined | null): boolean {
  if (isProdEnv(appEnv)) {
    return true;
  }
  const forwarded = forwardedProto(request.headers.get(FORWARDED_PROTO_HEADER));
  if (forwarded !== null) {
    return forwarded === 'https';
  }
  return new URL(request.url).protocol === 'https:';
}
```

## 7. CSRF / signed cookies / HMAC — definitive answer

**There is a CSRF module, but it holds no token. There is no signed cookie, no HMAC helper, and no crypto of any kind in `web/`.**

`web/src/lib/csrf.ts` exports exactly one function plus a private helper:

```ts
export function isSameOrigin(request: Request, siteOrigin: string): boolean
```

It compares the **host** of `Origin` (falling back to `Referer`) against the host of the site origin; a request with neither is refused. Host, not full origin, because `@astrojs/node` builds `Astro.url` from the socket (lines 26-51 explain at length). Its own docblock, lines 13-15, states the gap you are looking at:

```
 * The check goes in before real approvals exist rather than after, so
 * enabling auth cannot silently open the hole. It is a floor, not a
 * ceiling: a per-session token belongs here too once there are sessions
 * to bind one to.
```

Nine call sites: `pages/ops/{withdrawals,reconciliation,unattributed,held}.astro:14`, `pages/api/cashback/clickout.ts:5`, `pages/[lang]/signin.astro:7`, `pages/[lang]/editor/{audit,index,signin,sources}.astro`, `pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/withdraw.astro:26`. Usage pattern (`signin.astro:72-74`):

```ts
  if (!isSameOrigin(Astro.request, Astro.url.origin)) {
    return new Response('cross-origin sign-in refused', { status: 403 });
  }
```

**Absent, verified by grep across `web/src`:** `node:crypto`, `createHmac`, `timingSafeEqual`, `crypto.subtle`, `randomUUID`, `jose`, `jsonwebtoken`, `jwtVerify`. `web/package.json` dependencies are only `@astrojs/node`, `@supabase/ssr`, `astro`, `driver.js`.

**Implication for F1.4:** you have no signing primitive. Two honest options: (a) store the bearer token in the cookie verbatim, `httpOnly`, and let *the API* remain the only verifier — the cookie is a bearer credential, not an assertion, so it needs no signature of ours; (b) pull in `jose` to verify against `JWKS_URL` on the web side too, which duplicates a check the API already does. (a) matches the existing design (`resolveSession` never trusts cookie contents either — it round-trips to the auth server). If you go with (a), your exchange route must verify the token *once*, at exchange time, by calling the API (`GET /api/v1/account` with the bearer) and only minting the cookie on a 2xx — that is "confirms it" without any crypto in `web/`. Node 22 is the floor (`engines`), so `node:crypto` is available if you later need it.

```go
// mint signs an RS256 token for one subject. The claims are the ones the
// verifier actually checks - sub, iat, exp - and nothing more: a token
// carrying claims this deployment ignores would suggest they mattered.
func mint(key jwk.Key, subject uuid.UUID) (string, error) {
	now := time.Now()
	token, err := jwt.NewBuilder().
		Subject(subject.String()).
		IssuedAt(now.Add(-time.Minute)).
		Expiration(now.Add(tokenLifetime)).
		Build()
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	signed, err := jwt.Sign(token, jwt.WithKey(jwa.RS256(), key))
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return string(signed), nil
}
```

## 6. `web/src/lib/secure-request.ts`

Full file quoted in the read above. The two exports:

```ts
export const FORWARDED_PROTO_HEADER = 'x-forwarded-proto';

export function forwardedProto(raw: string | null | undefined): string | null {
  if (raw === null || raw === undefined) {
    return null;
  }
  const first = raw.split(',')[0]?.trim().toLowerCase() ?? '';
  return first === '' ? null : first;
}

export function isSecureRequest(request: Request, appEnv: string | undefined | null): boolean {
  if (isProdEnv(appEnv)) {
    return true;
  }
  const forwarded = forwardedProto(request.headers.get(FORWARDED_PROTO_HEADER));
  if (forwarded !== null) {
    return forwarded === 'https';
  }
  return new URL(request.url).protocol === 'https:';
}
```

Layering: `APP_ENV=prod` ⇒ `true` unconditionally; else `X-Forwarded-Proto`; else the request URL. Callers pass `APP_ENV` in — the module stays pure. In the demo (`APP_ENV=dev`, no proxy, `http://localhost:4321`) it returns `false`, so the cookie is set without `Secure` and the browser stores it. Exactly what you need.

Depends on `isProdEnv` from `web/src/lib/app-env.ts`:

```ts
export function parseAppEnv(raw: string | undefined | null): AppEnv | null {
  if (raw === undefined || raw === null || raw === '') { return APP_ENV_DEV; }
  if (raw === APP_ENV_DEV || raw === APP_ENV_PROD) { return raw; }
  return null;
}
export function isProdEnv(raw: string | undefined | null): boolean {
  return parseAppEnv(raw) === APP_ENV_PROD;
}
```
