`web/src/lib/csrf.ts` exports exactly one function plus a private helper:

```ts
export function isSameOrigin(request: Request, siteOrigin: string): boolean
```

It compares the **host** of `Origin` (falling back to `Referer`) against the host of the site origin; a request with neither is refused. Host, not full origin, because `@astrojs/node` builds `Astro.url` from the socket (lines 26-51 explain at length). Its own docblock, lines 13-15, states the gap you are looking at:

```
 * The check goes in before real approvals exist rather than after, so
 * enabling auth cannot silently open the hole. It is a floor, not a
 * ceiling: a per-session token belongs here too once there are sessions
 * to bind one to.
```

Nine call sites: `pages/ops/{withdrawals,reconciliation,unattributed,held}.astro:14`, `pages/api/cashback/clickout.ts:5`, `pages/[lang]/signin.astro:7`, `pages/[lang]/editor/{audit,index,signin,sources}.astro`, `pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/withdraw.astro:26`. Usage pattern (`signin.astro:72-74`):

```ts
  if (!isSameOrigin(Astro.request, Astro.url.origin)) {
    return new Response('cross-origin sign-in refused', { status: 403 });
  }
```

**Absent, verified by grep across `web/src`:** `node:crypto`, `createHmac`, `timingSafeEqual`, `crypto.subtle`, `randomUUID`, `jose`, `jsonwebtoken`, `jwtVerify`. `web/package.json` dependencies are only `@astrojs/node`, `@supabase/ssr`, `astro`, `driver.js`.

**Implication for F1.4:** you have no signing primitive. Two honest options: (a) store the bearer token in the cookie verbatim, `httpOnly`, and let *the API* remain the only verifier — the cookie is a bearer credential, not an assertion, so it needs no signature of ours; (b) pull in `jose` to verify against `JWKS_URL` on the web side too, which duplicates a check the API already does. (a) matches the existing design (`resolveSession` never trusts cookie contents either — it round-trips to the auth server). If you go with (a), your exchange route must verify the token *once*, at exchange time, by calling the API (`GET /api/v1/account` with the bearer) and only minting the cookie on a 2xx — that is "confirms it" without any crypto in `web/`. ## 7 — F1.4: the app-shell token exchange *(two PRs)*

This is what lets a browser be signed in with no Supabase project, which is
what F8's Playwright test needs. The survey turned up three facts that shape
it, and one that is a bug in the demo.

**`/auth/shell` needs no middleware change.** `isAccessPath` already matches
`/^\/auth(?:\/|$)/` (`middleware.ts:182-186`), so the route is already an
authenticated path, already gets `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, and a
shell session automatically satisfies `fenceCashback` because that reads
`sessionOf()` like everything else.

**There is no crypto in `web/`** — no `jose`, no `node:crypto`, no HMAC, no
signed cookie. That settles the design rather than blocking it: the cookie
holds the bearer token verbatim and **the api stays the only verifier**, which
is exactly what `resolveSession` already does (it never trusts cookie contents
either — it round-trips to the auth server). The exchange confirms the token
once by calling the api with it, and the session resolver confirms it again on
each request, parallel to Supabase's `getUser()` and at the same cost.

**`reader/preference.ts` is the template** for the cookie: a first-party,
non-Supabase cookie with a narrow `PreferenceCookieStore` interface that keeps
the module testable without Astro. It also records why `__Host-` was rejected —
it mandates `Secure` and the demo runs on plain http. Same trade here;
`isSecureRequest` decides `Secure`.

### 7a — the demo harness tells the truth *(shell + one Go line)*

Three defects, all of which would otherwise make F8 impossible:

1. **`API_BASE_URL` is never exported for the web**, so `answersFromFixtures`
   is true, the fence never fires and all four pages render fixtures. The
   demo's own closing text admits it. Exporting it is what turns the demo into
   a real end-to-end stack — and it is why the exchange has to land with it.
2. **`BRAND_DIR` is repo-relative** but `astro dev` runs with cwd `web/`, so it
   does not resolve for the web process. F3's opt-in reads the terms version
   from the brand, so this has to be right before F3 can be demonstrated.
3. **The minted token carries no `email` claim** (`scripts/demo/auth.go:231`),
   so `POST /api/v1/account` answers 400 — *"the token carries no email"*.
   `writeAccounts` already computes the address it writes
   (`<id>@demo.invalid`); emitting the same string as a claim keeps one fact
   one fact, and lets the exchange reuse `registerAccount` unchanged rather
   than growing a second code path for the demo's benefit.

### 7b — the exchange

- One new optional env flag in `web/astro.config.mjs`, in the house style
  (`envField.string`, never `envField.enum` — the file says why at lines 30-35).
- A pure `web/src/lib/member/shell-session.ts`: cookie name, options, the
  flag's truth test, and the mapping from an `Account` profile to a `Session`.
  `sessionFrom` will not serve — it maps Supabase claims — but
  `{id, email, display_name, role}` maps onto `Session` one to one, which also
  means **the role comes from the database row rather than a token claim**,
  which is what the api insists on.
- A thin `/auth/shell` route, modelled on `web/src/pages/auth/confirm.ts`:
  renders nothing, calls the api with the bearer, sets the cookie on success,
  303s to a `safeReturnPath`.
- A composite resolver in the middleware: shell cookie first (cheaper, and the
  flag gates it), Supabase second.

Note for whoever writes the tests: any test importing `middleware.ts` must add
the new key to its `vi.mock('astro:env/server', …)` object or it reads
`undefined`.

---

## Order

Housekeeping first, as asked, then the defect, then the path to a transaction.

| # | PR | Why here |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `.mcp.json` carries both servers, and the doc stops saying "a server" | founder's first ask, tiny |
| 2 | *(no PR)* stale issues closed, with a report | founder's second ask |
| 3 | the click-out endpoint's open redirect and its 500 | a real defect, and small |
| 4 | `/{lang}/terms` | F3a |
| 5 | the opt-in screen | F3b — the last thing between a member and a click |
| 6 | click-out: every band, and a sentence per outcome | F5b, needs 5 for the 403 |
| 7 | the catalogue reads its next page | F4 |
| 8 | the wallet's count, its paging and its `?entry=` | F6 |
| 9 | the demo harness tells the truth | F1.4a |
| 10 | the shell exchange | F1.4b, and F8 after it |

End to end, once 9 and 10 land — and this is the first time it will be real


3. **F3** — opt-in and the terms route, on my own judgement (settled: I draft

4. **F1.4 and F4/F5/F6** — planned and executed.

---

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "icepanel": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.icepanel.io/mcp" } } }
```

not a one-line edit: `docs/architecture/icepanel-model.md:2030` says the file
*"names a server and nothing else"*, and
`docs/architecture/README.md:85` points at it. The sentence stops being true
the moment a second server is added, so it changes in the same commit.

it — so there is no check to extend.

---

## 2 — Stale issues: close what the tree proves is built

The founder's read is right, and the evidence is entirely local — which
matters, because **GitHub's secondary rate limit is currently refusing this
account's content requests**, and any plan that needs one API call per issue
will stall. The method below needs two or three reads and one write per issue
actually closed.

### The evidence, gathered without the API

Three independent signals, all computable from the tree:

| Signal | How | Found |
|---|---|---|
| A commit on `main` names the issue | `git log --format=%s` → `(#N)` | **173 distinct numbers** |
| Code or config cites the issue | `git grep '#NNN'` over `internal/ web/src/ cmd/ scripts/ deploy/` | **83 numbers** |
| The artifact the issue names exists | issue title names a file/symbol; check the tree | per issue |

Intersecting that with the open-issue list is the candidate set.

### Why the obvious source is not usable

`specs/*/tasks.md` checkboxes look authoritative and are not.
`specs/002-apivo-cashback-alpha/tasks.md` reports 81 done / 66 open, yet
T001–T006 are all unchecked and all plainly built — the cashback config keys,
the `blnk`/`redis` compose services, the `cashback` CI job. The checkboxes
have the same drift the issues do. **Evidence comes from code and history,
never from a checkbox.**

### How each issue is judged

- **Tier A — close.** A commit subject on `main` carries `(#N)`. That is the
  repository's own convention for "this commit did that", and an issue still
  open under one was simply never referenced by a PR body. Closed with a
  comment citing the commits.
- **Tier B — verify, then close or leave.** No commit reference, but the title
  names a concrete artifact (`internal/cashback/payout/handlers.go`, a route,
  a symbol). Check the artifact and its tests. `#242` is the shape of this:
  no commit cites it, and every handler it asks for exists.
- **Tier C — leave open, and list.** Anything ambiguous, anything for an
  unbuilt feature (the `003-cashback-claims` backlog, #448–#492, is not
  built), and anything where the artifact exists but the issue asks for more
  than the artifact.

Tier C is reported to the founder rather than guessed at. A wrongly closed
issue is a task that quietly stops existing.

### Rate-limit discipline

Two or three reads to list the open issues, then all judgement is local. Each
close is one `PATCH` (`state: closed`, `state_reason: completed`) plus one
comment. Batched with pauses and resumable from a written work-list, so a
secondary limit part-way through costs nothing but time.

switcher as `/{lang}/impressum` — but **not** a fourth `LegalPane`.

jurisdiction); the cashback terms are prose, and forcing them through it would
distort a component that currently does one thing well.

Content lives in a new `web/src/lib/legal/terms.ts` beside
`lib/legal/strings.ts`, in `el` and `de`, with the version rendered from
`brand.legal.documents.terms.version` — the same field
`Participations.Join` compares (`internal/cashback/wallet/participations.go:162`).

Each clause states a rule the code actually enforces, and nothing else:

| Clause | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| the rate shown when you clicked is the rate that applies | FR-013, the band snapshotted onto the click |
| an entry is pending until the shop confirms it | `earnings/state.go` — `held pending confirmed reserved paid reversed` |
| a refund reverses it, and both rows stay visible | `reversal_of_id`, US3 scenario 2 |
| money is paid only to an account proved yours | FR-051, `verified_at` |
| there is a floor before a payout | `payout_threshold` |
| leaving stops the earning and keeps the records | FR-003 — a status and a date, never a deletion |
| balances are a claim on a future rebate | founder decision Q2, ADR-0002 |

No invented obligations, no boilerplate, and the PR says plainly that
counsel-approved text replaces this before launch.

**Not** linked from the site footer. That carries the three notices a
German-facing service legally owes; these are product terms, reached from the
opt-in screen and from the wallet.

contract says so. Posts `brand.legal.documents.terms.version`; a 400 means the
version moved under the member and the page reloads rather than re-posting a
stale consent; a 503 means the deployment names no brand (`ErrNoBrand`) and
the page says so rather than retrying.

here. `api.optIn()` has existed with zero call sites since it was written.

touches, and F1.4 touches `middleware.ts`, which #573 changes as well. So each
branches from `main` once #569 and #573 have merged, and stacks on them with
`gh stack` if they have not. Verified before branching, not assumed.

## 4 — F5: click-out, end to end *(two PRs, and one of them is a fix)*

The edge half is **done and proven**: `snippets.caddy:96` is now

asserts both halves — api routes to the api, `/api/cashback/clickout` and
`/api/tour/*` to the web, previews included.

### 4a — the click-out endpoint's own defects *(fix first)*

`web/src/pages/api/cashback/clickout.ts` has three, found while surveying:

1. **An open redirect on the failure path.** `back.startsWith('/')` admits
   `//evil.example`, which is protocol-relative and leaves the site. This
   repository already owns the correct check — `safeReturnPath`
   (`web/src/lib/member/access.ts`), written for exactly this in #564, which
   rejects it explicitly. Use it.
2. **`createCashbackApi` sits outside the `try`.** In `APP_ENV=prod` with no
   `API_BASE_URL` it throws a raw Astro 500 at a member mid-click instead of
   redirecting back with a status.
3. **`?` is appended unconditionally**, so the moment `back` carries a query

### 4b — the click-out a member can act on

Today `[slug].astro:97` reads the outcome with `.has()` and throws the value
away, so six distinct API answers collapse into one sentence
(`t.clickoutFailed`). The Go handler distinguishes them, and each wants a
different move from the member:

| Status | Means | What the page should say |
|---|---|---|
| **403** | **not opted in** — B3/#568 landed this while I was working | point at the opt-in screen; this is the one that is *actionable* |
| 429 | the click rule, with `Retry-After` | wait, and say roughly how long |
| 409 | band expired or retailer inactive | the offer is gone; the page reloads to show what is left |
| 502 | no deeplink could be built; **nothing was recorded** | try again, safely |
| 401 | no session | the fence handles it; belt and braces |
| 400 | a bad offer id | our fault, not theirs |

The 429's `Retry-After` is currently dropped by the web endpoint — only the
number `429` survives into the query string.

**Every published band gets a button.** `[slug].astro:105` takes
`merchant?.rates[0]` and only that one, so a retailer publishing two bands has
one a member cannot click at all. The rate table already renders them all and
each carries its own `offer_id`.

## 5 — F4: the catalogue on the real endpoint *(one PR)*

The endpoint is complete and its shape already matches `types.ts` field for
field. What is missing is on this side:

- **`next_cursor` is discarded** (`index.astro:70`) and there is no paging UI
  anywhere in this codebase to copy. The shelf is hard-capped at 20 because
  the client always sends `limit`, so the server's own default never applies.
- **`t.partnersCount(items.length, …)` presents 20 as the total.** The
  honest shape already exists: `allSources`

  returns a `truncated` flag, with `sources.astro` as the precedent for
  rendering it. Lift the shape, not the function.

  `page()` hard-codes `next_cursor: null`), so any control built here is dead
  in dev and on previews until the fixture honours a cursor.
- **An unknown place slug is a 400** and currently takes the whole page down
  as a 503 with `Retry-After: 60`.

  `t.sortedNote` carries the claim instead. Use one and delete the other —
  along with `noteColumn`, `confirmationTimeUnknown`, `merchantNotFound`,

  only the 20 loaded entries, so a member linked to their 21st entry is shown
  their 1st. That is the one to fix first.

  unfiltered and takes `.items.length`), so the count reads "20 of 20"
  forever. It also doubles the wallet's API traffic on every render.

---

what F8's Playwright test needs. The survey turned up three facts that shape
it, and one that is a bug in the demo.

`/^\/auth(?:\/|$)/` (`middleware.ts:182-186`), so the route is already an
authenticated path, already gets `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, and a
shell session automatically satisfies `fenceCashback` because that reads
`sessionOf()` like everything else.

signed cookie. That settles the design rather than blocking it: the cookie
holds the bearer token verbatim and **the api stays the only verifier**, which
is exactly what `resolveSession` already does (it never trusts cookie contents

once by calling the api with it, and the session resolver confirms it again on
each request, parallel to Supabase's `getUser()` and at the same cost.

non-Supabase cookie with a narrow `PreferenceCookieStore` interface that keeps
the module testable without Astro. It also records why `__Host-` was rejected —
it mandates `Secure` and the demo runs on plain http. Same trade here;
`isSecureRequest` decides `Secure`.

Three defects, all of which would otherwise make F8 impossible:

1. **`API_BASE_URL` is never exported for the web**, so `answersFromFixtures`
   is true, the fence never fires and all four pages render fixtures. The
   demo's own closing text admits it. Exporting it is what turns the demo into
   a real end-to-end stack — and it is why the exchange has to land with it.
2. **`BRAND_DIR` is repo-relative** but `astro dev` runs with cwd `web/`, so it
   does not resolve for the web process. F3's opt-in reads the terms version
   from the brand, so this has to be right before F3 can be demonstrated.

   so `POST /api/v1/account` answers 400 — *"the token carries no email"*.
   `writeAccounts` already computes the address it writes
   (`<id>@demo.invalid`); emitting the same string as a claim keeps one fact
   one fact, and lets the exchange reuse `registerAccount` unchanged rather
   than growing a second code path for the demo's benefit.

- One new optional env flag in `web/astro.config.mjs`, in the house style
  (`envField.string`, never `envField.enum` — the file says why at lines 30-35).
- A pure `web/src/lib/member/shell-session.ts`: cookie name, options, the
  flag's truth test, and the mapping from an `Account` profile to a `Session`.
  `sessionFrom` will not serve — it maps Supabase claims — but
  `{id, email, display_name, role}` maps onto `Session` one to one, which also
  means **the role comes from the database row rather than a token claim**,
  which is what the api insists on.
- A thin `/auth/shell` route, modelled on `web/src/pages/auth/confirm.ts`:
  renders nothing, calls the api with the bearer, sets the cookie on success,
  303s to a `safeReturnPath`.
- A composite resolver in the middleware: shell cookie first (cheaper, and the
  flag gates it), Supabase second.

Note for whoever writes the tests: any test importing `middleware.ts` must add
the new key to its `vi.mock('astro:env/server', …)` object or it reads
`undefined`.

---

Housekeeping first, as asked, then the defect, then the path to a transaction.

| # | PR | Why here |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `.mcp.json` carries both servers, and the doc stops saying "a server" | founder's first ask, tiny |

| 8 | the wallet's count, its paging and its `?entry=` | F6 |
| 9 | the demo harness tells the truth | F1.4a |

## Verification

Per PR, the gates that already exist:


must join `web/vitest.config.ts`'s coverage `include` or it escapes the gate
silently.

End to end, once 9 and 10 land — and this is the first time it will be real
rather than fixtures:

```sh

# sign in through /auth/shell with $TMP/reader.token, opt in, open a
# retailer, click out, read the wallet
```

The issue cleanup is written to survive that: two or three reads, all
judgement local, one write per issue closed, batched with pauses and resumable
from a written work-list.

Yes, enabled — but I should give you an honest number rather than a flattering one.

**What's enabled:** the index is committed (`graft/`, 620 cards), the CLI is on PATH, there's a skill and a SessionStart hook, and the MCP tools were available this session as deferred tools. After the commit I just made, `.mcp.json` carries both graft and IcePanel, so future sessions get the MCP server too rather than depending on whose checkout you're in.

**Tokens saved this session: ~86k, from exactly one subagent.**

That's the whole tally, and the breakdown is not flattering:

| Who | graft tally |
|---|---|
| The auth/session survey | **~86,008 saved** — its own report |
| The catalogue/click-out/wallet survey | ~0 — *"the task named every file to read"* |
| The shell-exchange survey | ~0 — same reason |
| The design-canvas extraction | n/a — a 3MB HTML artifact, not source |
| **Me, directly** | **zero. I never called a graft tool.** |

I used `git grep`, `git log` and `sed` throughout. The repo's own guidance says to reach for graft first and I mostly didn't — which is a bit rich given I just wrote a commit message arguing for its place in the config.

The reason the last two agents saved nothing is instructive though, and not really a failure: I'd already located everything, so their prompts named exact files. graft's value is in *finding* code, and by then there was nothing left to find. The 86k came from the one survey where I genuinely didn't know where the auth seam lived.

Where it would have earned its keep and I skipped it: tracing `EditorSession` across 28 files for the rename (I used `git grep -l` then read each), and mapping the click-out failure paths. `graft callers` is exactly the tool for the first — the guidance even says to run it before a rename, and I didn't.

I'll use it properly for the remaining work — the click-out statuses and the wallet paging both start from "where does this actually go", which is its case.

The `.mcp.json` commit is made; let me finish that PR and move to the issue cleanup.

You were right, and I wasn't testing in the browser. I am now.

## What was actually wrong

Your browser is signed in as `editor1@example.com` — visible in the editor chrome. The chain:

1. Reader pages **deliberately resolve no session** (it costs an auth round-trip, and the front page is most of the traffic), so the chrome shows "Σύνδεση" to everyone — including you.
2. Clicking it goes to `/el/signin`, which found your session and **silently redirected you back where you came from**.
3. The page you were on is the page you ended up on. The button does nothing.

I reproduced it exactly: with `?next=/el/munich` it bounced to `/el/munich`; with no `next` it bounced to `/el/munich+greece` — both precisely the redirect target in my code.

## Why my tests said it was fine

This is the part worth dwelling on. `curl https://ra1ze.com/el/signin` returns **200 with a working form** — the page is genuinely correct for a signed-out visitor. And `signin.test.ts` rendered through the container with no session, because the middleware that files one doesn't run there.

**Every one of my 27 cases tested the one visitor the page was already right for.** The redirect branch shipped completely unexercised. A hundred percent of the tests passing told me nothing about the state you were in.

## Fixed — [#584](https://github.com/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/pull/584)

The page now says who's signed in, offers a way onward, and offers sign-out (which is how you sign in as someone else). The two sign-in paths are *rendered away*, not hidden — a form in the DOM is a form that can be posted. Signing out lands back on the sign-in page and says so.

The harness can now file a session by hand (`rememberSession` is exported, the WeakMap is keyed by the request), and four new cases cover the branch. 1052 tests pass.

**Still wrong, and I've left it deliberately:** the chrome offers "sign in" to someone signed in. That's the root cause, and fixing it means either paying for a session on reader pages or a lighter-weight hint. It belongs with the member-bar work — #584 makes the product honest either way.

content.content:
name: preview

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, closed]

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  # Per pull request, and cancellable: pushing three times in a minute should
  # build the third one, not all three. This is the opposite choice from
  # publish.yml, because nothing here can leave a channel half-moved - the
  # worst a cancelled preview build does is leave the previous preview up.
  group: preview-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Closed: delete the tags. The host does the rest.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  teardown:
    # Same fork restriction as `publish` below, for the same reason and with
    # the same consequence: a fork pull request never published preview tags,
    # so there is nothing to delete when it closes.
    if: >-
      github.event.action == 'closed' &&
      github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - name: Delete this pull request's image tags
        env:
          # A personal access token with `delete:packages` when one is
          # configured, and the automatic token otherwise.
          #
          # GITHUB_TOKEN publishes package versions perfectly well and often
          # CANNOT DELETE THEM: `packages: write` covers the push, while the
          # delete endpoint wants a token with `delete:packages` and admin on
          # the package. That is what failed the first time this ran for
          # real — the listing succeeded, the delete did not.
          #
          # The fallback is deliberate rather than a hard requirement: a
          # repository with no PAT still publishes previews, and only loses
          # exact teardown.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PREVIEW_CLEANUP_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          USING_PAT: ${{ secrets.PREVIEW_CLEANUP_TOKEN != '' }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}

The founder's correction (2026-09-07): **do not wait for code to reach `main`/QA to
click it — every PR gets an ephemeral preview at `pr-<n>.ra1ze.com`, and that is where
frontend work is verified.** They caught a shipped bug (#583, the sign-in button doing
nothing) by clicking QA, after I had merged three PRs on green CI without ever opening a
browser.

**Why:** unit tests here render through the Astro container, where the middleware does
not run — so any branch that depends on a resolved session is untested by construction,
and `curl` misses the same class because it carries no cookies. A browser on a preview is
the only thing that exercises the signed-in paths.

**How to apply.** `preview.yml` builds `pr-<n>` images on `pull_request`
(opened/synchronize/reopened); `deploy/hetzner/bin/apivo-previews` reconciles every
minute off those registry tags. So a preview is clickable a couple of minutes after
opening a PR — poll `https://pr-<n>.ra1ze.com/` with curl rather than the GitHub API,
which is frequently secondary-rate-limited on this account. 502 means the tag is not
published yet.

**What a preview can and cannot prove:**

- **CAN**: sign-in, the editorial screens, layout, copy, anything session-shaped.
  `docker-compose.preview.yml` gives the web container real `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_*` sharing
  QA's nonprod project, and the reconciler copies QA's editor account rows into the
  preview's own database.
- **CANNOT**: cashback *integration*. `PUBLIC_APP_VERSION` is the `pr-<n>` tag, and
  `isPreviewVersion` (`web/src/lib/cashback/api.ts:452`) matches `/^pr-\d+$/`, so
  `answersFromFixtures` is true and every cashback surface answers from built-in
  fixtures. Live entries, the click-out and the sign-in fence still need QA.

`CASHBACK_PREVIEW_FIXTURES: "1"` in `docker-compose.preview.yml` is **dead config** —
read nowhere in `web/`, though its comment claims it is what makes the pages render
fixtures. The version stamp is the live mechanism. Worth deleting.

See [[apivo-news-project]] and [[apivo-news-working-style]].

Understood — and you're right that I should have been on the previews from the start. I've set that up and found something worth telling you.

## The mechanism, confirmed

`preview.yml` builds `pr-<n>` images on every PR; `apivo-previews` reconciles every minute off those registry tags. **Both my preview builds succeeded** — `signin-answers-the-signed-in` at 18:17, `mcp-graft-beside-icepanel` at 18:20.

## But both previews are 502

`pr-582.ra1ze.com` and `pr-584.ra1ze.com` both return 502 on `/` and `/el/signin`, while `ra1ze.com` returns 200. So the images are published and the edge knows the hosts, but the containers aren't serving. It isn't the concurrency cap — that keeps the five *highest-numbered* PRs and mine are at the top. I have a watcher polling; I'll report when they answer.

Worth flagging since it means the preview lane is currently not usable, which is presumably not the intent.

## What a preview can and can't prove

This turned out to matter more than I expected:

- **Can**: sign-in, editorial screens, layout, anything session-shaped. `docker-compose.preview.yml` gives the web container real `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_*` sharing QA's nonprod project, and the reconciler copies QA's editor rows into the preview's own database. **So #584's bug — the signed-in bounce — is exactly a preview-testable thing.** I should have caught it there.
- **Can't**: cashback *integration*. `PUBLIC_APP_VERSION` is `pr-<n>`, `isPreviewVersion` matches `/^pr-\d+$/`, so `answersFromFixtures` is true and every cashback surface answers from fixtures. Live entries, the click-out and the sign-in fence still need QA.

That split is now in my memory so I stop conflating the two.

## One thing I found while checking

`docker-compose.preview.yml` sets `CASHBACK_PREVIEW_FIXTURES: "1"` with a long comment explaining it's what makes the cashback pages render fixtures. **It's read nowhere in `web/`** — dead config. The live mechanism is the version stamp. Harmless today, but the comment will mislead whoever next tries to change preview behaviour. I'll fold the deletion into a housekeeping PR unless you'd rather it stayed.

I did verify my fence exemption is genuinely correct on previews (`pr-584` → fixtures → exempt), so reviewers won't get redirected away from the cashback screens.

## Where things stand

- [#582](https://github.com/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/pull/582) — `.mcp.json` carries graft beside IcePanel
- [#584](https://github.comty/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/pull/584) — the sign-in fix, with tests that file a session by hand so the branch that shipped unexercised now isn't

Once the previews come up I'll click through #584 as a signed-in user and confirm it behaves, before asking you to merge. The stale-issue cleanup is still blocked on GitHub's secondary rate limit.

content.text:
No — I checked in the browser, not just curl, and it's genuinely down.

Cloudflare's own error page at **18:33:29 UTC**: `Browser ✅ → Cloudflare ✅ → Host ❌`. Same for `pr-582`. Meanwhile `ra1ze.com` serves 200, so the box and Caddy are fine — it's the preview containers specifically.

## What I can establish from here

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `preview.yml` build for #584 | **success**, 18:17:51 |
| `preview.yml` build for #582 | **success**, 18:20:20 |
| Concurrency cap | not it — keeps the 5 *highest-numbered* PRs, mine are top |
| QA origin | healthy |
| Preview origin | not answering, both PRs |

So the images built. What I can't see from here is whether they reached the registry or whether the host started them — `gh` can't read package versions (the token lacks `read:packages`), and I have no host access.

The Caddy preview block dials `apivo-pr-<n>-web:4321` by name, so a 502 on a wildcard preview host means that container isn't running. Three candidates, in the order the reconciler itself would fail:

1. **Registry credential expired** — the script has an explicit death for this: *"cannot list preview tags … the registry is unreachable or the credential has expired (docker login ghcr.io). No preview was created or destroyed."*
2. **The timer isn't running** — `apivo-previews.timer` should fire every 60s.
3. **Stack creation failed** — preview database, or the shared frontend certificate at `/etc/apivo/preview/web-certs` (the script warns that without it *"every preview's web container would crash-loop rather than serve"*).

On the host, in that order:

```sh
systemctl status apivo-previews.timer apivo-previews.service
journalctl -u apivo-previews.service -n 50 --no-pager
docker ps -a --filter 'name=apivo-pr-'
ls -l /etc/apivo/preview/web-certs/
```

The reconciler logs structured JSON, so `journalctl` should name the failure directly.

## Where that leaves the two PRs

Both are code-complete and green; neither has been clicked. [#584](https://github.com/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/pull/584) is the one that matters — it's the fix for the button you found, and the signed-in branch is exactly what a preview would prove and unit tests structurally cannot. I'd rather not ask you to merge it unverified, given that's precisely how the original bug shipped.

Two options: you look at the host and I test on the preview once it's back; or you merge #584 and I verify on QA within the two-minute deploy and revert immediately if it's wrong. Your call — but if previews are broken for everyone, that's worth knowing independently of my PRs, since the backend team is landing several a day and the preview lane is where those get reviewed too.

My watcher is still polling `pr-584` and I'll pick it up the moment it answers.

QA is still on `2fe3fe1` (#585); my watcher will catch #584 when it rolls. Meanwhile, here's the picture.

## Where the frontend journey stands

The goal is one real transaction: sign up → opt in → click out → a pending entry.

| | Item | State |
|---|---|---|
| — | Contract truth (types vs api) | ✅ merged #561 — wasn't on the list, but the withdrawal screen was broken without it |
| F1.1 | Session groundwork | ✅ merged #563 |
| F1.2 | Email link sign-in | ✅ merged #565 |
| F1.3 | Account provisioning | ✅ merged #569 |
| F1.5 | Sign-out | ✅ merged #584 (arrived early, with the fix you found) |
| F2 | Gating | ✅ merged #573 |
| **F3** | **Opt-in + terms** | ⛔ **not started — the last frontend blocker** |
| F4 | Catalogue paging | endpoint live; frontend discards `next_cursor` |
| F5 | Click-out | edge fixed; 3 endpoint defects + per-status copy outstanding |
| F6 | Wallet | 3 defects, one a correctness bug |
| F1.4 | Shell exchange | planned, not built |
| F7 | Payout destination | not started |
| F8 | Browser test | not started, needs F1.4 |

**F3 is now the only thing between here and a member completing the journey.** That got sharper while I was working: the backend landed B3 (#568), so the click-out now returns 403 to anyone who hasn't opted in — and there is no screen to opt in with. `api.optIn()` has existed with zero call sites since it was written.

So F3 is what I do next, unless you say otherwise.

## Housekeeping — done

**Stale issues: 143 → 99.** I closed **19**, each with a comment citing the commits that did the work.

The method was evidence from the tree, not checkboxes — `specs/002/tasks.md` claims 81 done / 66 open, yet T001–T006 are unchecked and plainly built, so the checkboxes have exactly the same drift the issues do.

Five candidates I **deliberately did not close**, because a commit referencing an issue isn't proof it's finished:

- **#132** — a commit gave container renders a timeout, but I confirmed *today* that `astro-url-scheme.test.ts` still times out. Still live.
- **#206** — two of its three routes exist; `POST /ops/unattributed/{id}/attribute` does not. The frontend already calls it, so an operator can press a button that 404s. Noted on the issue; same shape as #545 and #556.
- **#275** — the backend half of the brand lint reached zero; **23 budget lines remain under `web/`**. Noted with the count.
- **#117**, **#524** — genuinely ambiguous (a deadlock that may or may not be fixed; a question for Linkwise). Left for you.

**`.mcp.json`** — [#582](https://github.com/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/pull/582) is open and green: graft beside IcePanel, plus the architecture doc sentence that claimed the file "names a server and nothing else".

## One thing I'd flag

While checking previews I found `CASHBACK_PREVIEW_FIXTURES: "1"` in `docker-compose.preview.yml`, with a long comment explaining it's what makes cashback render fixtures. **It's read nowhere in `web/`.** The live mechanism is the `pr-<n>` version stamp. Harmless now, misleading later — I'll delete it in a housekeeping PR unless you want it kept.

I'll verify #584 on QA the moment it deploys, then start F3.

input.description: Gather enforced cashback rules
input.prompt:
Repo: C:\Users\madym\repos\apivo-news — a Go modular monolith (`internal/cashback/...`) plus an Astro frontend. Read-only research on the CURRENT working tree.

I am writing a member-facing **cashback terms page**. Every clause must state a rule the code actually enforces, with nothing invented. I need each candidate clause verified against the implementation, with `file:line` citations I can put in a PR.

For each of the following, tell me **whether it is true, how it is enforced, and where** — quote the enforcing code or constraint:

1. **The rate that applied when the member clicked is the rate that governs the credit**, and a later rate change does not alter it. (I believe FR-013, a band snapshotted onto the click.) Where is the snapshot written, and what reads it back when an entry is opened?

2. **An entry is pending until the network confirms it.** What are the exact states and the legal transitions? (`internal/cashback/earnings/state.go` and the migration's check constraint.) Which states count toward a spendable balance and which do not?

3. **A refund reverses the credit, and both rows remain visible.** How is a reversal represented, is the original row ever mutated or deleted, and what guarantees both are returned to the member?

4. **Money is paid only to a destination the member has proved is theirs.** Where is an unverified destination refused, and with what status/code? (FR-051.)

5. **There is a minimum before a payout.** Where does the threshold come from (config? brand?), and where is a request below it refused, with what status and what figures in the problem document?

6. **Every payout is approved by a named human** — C-4. Where is that enforced: application code, or a database constraint? Quote the constraint if it is in a migration.

7. **Leaving cashback stops future earning and keeps the financial records.** What does `DELETE /participation` actually do to rows? Does anything cascade or delete?

8. **A balance is a claim on a future rebate, not money held for the member** — founder decision Q2 / ADR-0002. Where is that recorded, and is anything in the code shaped by it (e.g. no transfers between members, no in-app spending)?

9. **Opting in records which version of the terms was accepted**, and a stale version is refused. Quote the check.

10. **Amounts are integer minor units with an explicit currency**, never a float (C-6). Where is that enforced on the wire and in the database?

11. Anything the code enforces that a member would want to know and that I have NOT listed — especially anything about a click expiring, a hold rule keeping money out of a balance, or a currency the member cannot be paid in. Recent commits mention `#577` (entry currency) and `#579` (a click carrying its network) — say what those changed if it affects what a member should be told.

Answer clause by clause. Where something is NOT enforced, or is weaker than I stated, say so plainly — I would rather drop a clause than write one the code does not back.

input.content:
# F3 — the terms, and the opt-in

## Context

A member can now sign up, sign in and become an account (#565, #569), and no
cashback page renders for a stranger (#573). **They cannot opt in**, so they
cannot click out — the backend landed B3 (#568) while this work was going on,
and `POST /clickouts` now answers **403** to anybody without a participation.
`api.optIn()` has existed with zero call sites since it was written.

So F3 is the last frontend blocker on the path to one real transaction:
sign up → **opt in** → click out → a pending entry.

Two PRs. The founder settled the open question earlier: **I draft the terms as
a statement of what the code enforces**, each clause traceable to a mechanism,
with the PR saying plainly that counsel-approved text replaces it before
launch.

### Done since the last plan (not repeated below)

`.mcp.json` carries both servers (#582, merged). The stale-issue sweep is
finished: 143 open → 99, nineteen closed with commit evidence, five left open
deliberately with the reasons recorded on #206 and #275. Both are off this
plan.

---

## Route decisions

**`/{lang}/terms`** — free; `/{lang}/` currently holds `about`, `contact`,
`faq`, `impressum`, `legal`, `privacy`, `register`, `setup`, `signin`.

**`/{lang}/{place}/cashback/join`** for the opt-in. A static segment beside
`[slug].astro`, which Astro resolves before the dynamic one — the same trade
`wallet` and `withdraw` already make, and `lib/cashback/paths.ts` documents
it: a retailer whose slug is `join` becomes unreachable rather than shadowing
the page. `join` is chosen over `opt-in` partly because a hyphen is a legal
merchant slug and a bare word is less likely to collide.

**Naming to keep apart:** `t.seeTerms` in the cashback catalogue is the
*retailer's* own conditions. This page is the *programme's* terms. Neither
string should drift into the other's job.

*(remaining sections pending survey results)*

+the page. `join` is chosen over `opt-in` partly because a hyphen is a legal
+merchant slug and a bare word is less likely to collide.
-Three independent signals, all computable from the tree:
+**Naming to keep apart:** `t.seeTerms` in the cashback catalogue is the
+*retailer's* own conditions. This page is the *programme's* terms. Neither
+string should drift into the other's job.
-| Signal | How | Found |
-| A commit on `main` names the issue | `git log --format=%s` → `(#N)` | **173 distinct numbers** |
-| Code or config cites the issue | `git grep '#NNN'` over `internal/ web/src/ cmd/ scripts/ deploy/` | **83 numbers** |
-| The artifact the issue names exists | issue title names a file/symbol; check the tree | per issue |
-Union of the first two: **197 issue numbers with implementation evidence.**

-### Why the obvious source is not usable
-`specs/*/tasks.md` checkboxes look authoritative and are not.
-`specs/002-apivo-cashback-alpha/tasks.md` reports 81 done / 66 open, yet
-T001–T006 are all unchecked and all plainly built — the cashback config keys,
-the `blnk`/`redis` compose services, the `cashback` CI job. The checkboxes
-have the same drift the issues do. **Evidence comes from code and history,
-never from a checkbox.**

-  repository's own convention for "this commit did that", and an issue still
-  open under one was simply never referenced by a PR body. Closed with a
-  comment citing the commits.
-- **Tier B — verify, then close or leave.** No commit reference, but the title
-  names a concrete artifact (`internal/cashback/payout/handlers.go`, a route,
-  a symbol). Check the artifact and its tests. `#242` is the shape of this:
-  no commit cites it, and every handler it asks for exists.
-- **Tier C — leave open, and list.** Anything ambiguous, anything for an
-  unbuilt feature (the `003-cashback-claims` backlog, #448–#492, is not
-  built), and anything where the artifact exists but the issue asks for more
-  than the artifact.
-Tier C is reported to the founder rather than guessed at. A wrongly closed
-issue is a task that quietly stops existing.
-### Rate-limit discipline
-Two or three reads to list the open issues, then all judgement is local. Each
-close is one `PATCH` (`state: closed`, `state_reason: completed`) plus one
-comment. Batched with pauses and resumable from a written work-list, so a
-secondary limit part-way through costs nothing but time.
-## 3 — F3: the terms, and the opt-in *(two PRs)*
-### 3a — `/{lang}/terms`
-Its own route in the legal family — same layout, masthead and language
-switcher as `/{lang}/impressum` — but **not** a fourth `LegalPane`.
-`LegalPane` renders term/value pairs out of `brand.legal` (entity, address,
-jurisdiction); the cashback terms are prose, and forcing them through it would
-distort a component that currently does one thing well.
-Content lives in a new `web/src/lib/legal/terms.ts` beside
-`lib/legal/strings.ts`, in `el` and `de`, with the version rendered from
-`brand.legal.documents.terms.version` — the same field
-`Participations.Join` compares (`internal/cashback/wallet/participations.go:162`).
-Each clause states a rule the code actually enforces, and nothing else:
-| Clause | Mechanism |
-| the rate shown when you clicked is the rate that applies | FR-013, the band snapshotted onto the click |
-| an entry is pending until the shop confirms it | `earnings/state.go` — `held pending confirmed reserved paid reversed` |
-| a refund reverses it, and both rows stay visible | `reversal_of_id`, US3 scenario 2 |
-| money is paid only to an account proved yours | FR-051, `verified_at` |
-| there is a floor before a payout | `payout_threshold` |
-| leaving stops the earning and keeps the records | FR-003 — a status and a date, never a deletion |
-| balances are a claim on a future rebate | founder decision Q2, ADR-0002 |
-No invented obligations, no boilerplate, and the PR says plainly that
-counsel-approved text replaces this before launch.
-**Not** linked from the site footer. That carries the three notices a
-German-facing service legally owes; these are product terms, reached from the
-opt-in screen and from the wallet.
-### 3b — the opt-in screen
-Reached when `GET /participation` answers 404 — which is not an error, and the
-contract says so. Posts `brand.legal.documents.terms.version`; a 400 means the
-version moved under the member and the page reloads rather than re-posting a
-stale consent; a 503 means the deployment names no brand (`ErrNoBrand`) and
-the page says so rather than retrying.
-The wallet's not-participating band stops pointing at the catalogue and points
-here. `api.optIn()` has existed with zero call sites since it was written.
-### Branch order
-F3 touches `wallet.astro` and `i18n/cashback.ts`, both of which #573 also
-touches, and F1.4 touches `middleware.ts`, which #573 changes as well. So each
-branches from `main` once #569 and #573 have merged, and stacks on them with
-`gh stack` if they have not. Verified before branching, not assumed.
-## 4 — F5: click-out, end to end *(two PRs, and one of them is a fix)*
-The edge half is **done and proven**: `snippets.caddy:96` is now
-`@api path /api/v1/* /healthz /readyz`, and `deploy/hetzner/validate.sh:646,658`
-asserts both halves — api routes to the api, `/api/cashback/clickout` and
-`/api/tour/*` to the web, previews included.
-### 4a — the click-out endpoint's own defects *(fix first)*
-`web/src/pages/api/cashback/clickout.ts` has three, found while surveying:
-1. **An open redirect on the failure path.** `back.startsWith('/')` admits
-   `//evil.example`, which is protocol-relative and leaves the site. This
-   repository already owns the correct check — `safeReturnPath`
-   (`web/src/lib/member/access.ts`), written for exactly this in #564, which
-   rejects it explicitly. Use it.
-2. **`createCashbackApi` sits outside the `try`.** In `APP_ENV=prod` with no
-   `API_BASE_URL` it throws a raw Astro 500 at a member mid-click instead of
-   redirecting back with a status.
-3. **`?` is appended unconditionally**, so the moment `back` carries a query
-   it builds `…?a=1?clickout=409`.
-### 4b — the click-out a member can act on
-Today `[slug].astro:97` reads the outcome with `.has()` and throws the value
-away, so six distinct API answers collapse into one sentence
-(`t.clickoutFailed`). The Go handler distinguishes them, and each wants a
-different move from the member:
-| Status | Means | What the page should say |
-| **403** | **not opted in** — B3/#568 landed this while I was working | point at the opt-in screen; this is the one that is *actionable* |
-| 429 | the click rule, with `Retry-After` | wait, and say roughly how long |
-| 409 | band expired or retailer inactive | the offer is gone; the page reloads to show what is left |
-| 502 | no deeplink could be built; **nothing was recorded** | try again, safely |
-| 401 | no session | the fence handles it; belt and braces |
-| 400 | a bad offer id | our fault, not theirs |
-The 429's `Retry-After` is currently dropped by the web endpoint — only the
-number `429` survives into the query string.
-**Every published band gets a button.** `[slug].astro:105` takes
-`merchant?.rates[0]` and only that one, so a retailer publishing two bands has
-one a member cannot click at all. The rate table already renders them all and
-each carries its own `offer_id`.

-The endpoint is complete and its shape already matches `types.ts` field for
-field. What is missing is on this side:

-  anywhere in this codebase to copy. The shelf is hard-capped at 20 because
-  the client always sends `limit`, so the server's own default never applies.
-- **`t.partnersCount(items.length, …)` presents 20 as the total.** The
-  honest shape already exists: `allSources`
-  (`web/src/lib/editorial/api.ts:911-940`) follows a cursor to a bound and
-  returns a `truncated` flag, with `sources.astro` as the precedent for
-  rendering it. Lift the shape, not the function.
-- **The fixture client cannot paginate** (`api.ts:193-202` ignores `cursor`,
-  `page()` hard-codes `next_cursor: null`), so any control built here is dead
-  in dev and on previews until the fixture honours a cursor.
-- **An unknown place slug is a 400** and currently takes the whole page down
-  as a 503 with `Retry-After: 60`.
-- `t.placementNotForSale` is defined in both languages and rendered nowhere;
-  `t.sortedNote` carries the claim instead. Use one and delete the other —
-  along with `noteColumn`, `confirmationTimeUnknown`, `merchantNotFound`,
-  `reservedExplained` and `payoutThreshold`, all defined and never rendered.
-## 6 — F6: the wallet against real entries *(one PR)*
-Three defects, one of them a correctness bug rather than a cosmetic one:
-- **`?entry=<id>` silently resolves against page one.** `explicit` searches
-  only the 20 loaded entries, so a member linked to their 21st entry is shown
-  their 1st. That is the one to fix first.
-- **`allCount` is `min(total, 20)`** (`wallet.astro:101` calls `api.entries()`
-  unfiltered and takes `.items.length`), so the count reads "20 of 20"
-  forever. It also doubles the wallet's API traffic on every render.
-- **`lang` is never sent on `entries()`**, so `merchant_name_is_fallback` is
-  true for every row and the wallet prints "shown in <language>" on all of
-  them. A one-line addition to `EntryQuery`.
-`GET /wallet/entries` is already cursor-complete server-side and needs no Go
-change.
-## 7 — F1.4: the app-shell token exchange *(two PRs)*
-This is what lets a browser be signed in with no Supabase project, which is
-what F8's Playwright test needs. The survey turned up three facts that shape
-it, and one that is a bug in the demo.
-**`/auth/shell` needs no middleware change.** `isAccessPath` already matches
-`/^\/auth(?:\/|$)/` (`middleware.ts:182-186`), so the route is already an
-authenticated path, already gets `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, and a
-shell session automatically satisfies `fenceCashback` because that reads
-`sessionOf()` like everything else.
-**There is no crypto in `web/`** — no `jose`, no `node:crypto`, no HMAC, no
-signed cookie. That settles the design rather than blocking it: the cookie
-holds the bearer token verbatim and **the api stays the only verifier**, which
-is exactly what `resolveSession` already does (it never trusts cookie contents
-either — it round-trips to the auth server). The exchange confirms the token
-once by calling the api with it, and the session resolver confirms it again on
-each request, parallel to Supabase's `getUser()` and at the same cost.
-**`reader/preference.ts` is the template** for the cookie: a first-party,
-non-Supabase cookie with a narrow `PreferenceCookieStore` interface that keeps
-the module testable without Astro. It also records why `__Host-` was rejected —
-it mandates `Secure` and the demo runs on plain http. Same trade here;
-`isSecureRequest` decides `Secure`.

-Three defects, all of which would otherwise make F8 impossible:
-1. **`API_BASE_URL` is never exported for the web**, so `answersFromFixtures`
-   is true, the fence never fires and all four pages render fixtures. The
-   demo's own closing text admits it. Exporting it is what turns the demo into
-   a real end-to-end stack — and it is why the exchange has to land with it.
-2. **`BRAND_DIR` is repo-relative** but `astro dev` runs with cwd `web/`, so it
-   does not resolve for the web process. F3's opt-in reads the terms version
-   from the brand, so this has to be right before F3 can be demonstrated.
-3. **The minted token carries no `email` claim** (`scripts/demo/auth.go:231`),
-   so `POST /api/v1/account` answers 400 — *"the token carries no email"*.
-   `writeAccounts` already computes the address it writes
-   (`<id>@demo.invalid`); emitting the same string as a claim keeps one fact
-   one fact, and lets the exchange reuse `registerAccount` unchanged rather
-   than growing a second code path for the demo's benefit.
-### 7b — the exchange
-- One new optional env flag in `web/astro.config.mjs`, in the house style
-  (`envField.string`, never `envField.enum` — the file says why at lines 30-35).
-- A pure `web/src/lib/member/shell-session.ts`: cookie name, options, the
-  flag's truth test, and the mapping from an `Account` profile to a `Session`.
-  `sessionFrom` will not serve — it maps Supabase claims — but
-  `{id, email, display_name, role}` maps onto `Session` one to one, which also
-  means **the role comes from the database row rather than a token claim**,
-  which is what the api insists on.
-- A thin `/auth/shell` route, modelled on `web/src/pages/auth/confirm.ts`:
-  renders nothing, calls the api with the bearer, sets the cookie on success,
-  303s to a `safeReturnPath`.
-- A composite resolver in the middleware: shell cookie first (cheaper, and the
-  flag gates it), Supabase second.
-Note for whoever writes the tests: any test importing `middleware.ts` must add
-the new key to its `vi.mock('astro:env/server', …)` object or it reads
-`undefined`.

-| # | PR | Why here |
-| 1 | `.mcp.json` carries both servers, and the doc stops saying "a server" | founder's first ask, tiny |
-| 2 | *(no PR)* stale issues closed, with a report | founder's second ask |
-| 3 | the click-out endpoint's open redirect and its 500 | a real defect, and small |
-| 4 | `/{lang}/terms` | F3a |

# F3 — the terms, and the opt-in

## Context

A member can now sign up, sign in and become an account (#565, #569), and no
cashback page renders for a stranger (#573). **They cannot opt in**, so they
cannot click out — the backend landed B3 (#568) while this work was going on,
and `POST /clickouts` now answers **403** to anybody without a participation.
`api.optIn()` has existed with zero call sites since it was written.

So F3 is the last frontend blocker on the path to one real transaction:
sign up → **opt in** → click out → a pending entry.

Two PRs. The founder settled the open question earlier: **I draft the terms as
a statement of what the code enforces**, each clause traceable to a mechanism,
with the PR saying plainly that counsel-approved text replaces it before
launch.

### Done since the last plan (not repeated below)

`.mcp.json` carries both servers (#582, merged). The stale-issue sweep is
finished: 143 open → 99, nineteen closed with commit evidence, five left open
deliberately with the reasons recorded on #206 and #275. Both are off this
plan.

---

## Route decisions

**`/{lang}/terms`** — free; `/{lang}/` currently holds `about`, `contact`,
`faq`, `impressum`, `legal`, `privacy`, `register`, `setup`, `signin`.

**`/{lang}/{place}/cashback/join`** for the opt-in. A static segment beside
`[slug].astro`, which Astro resolves before the dynamic one — the same trade
`wallet` and `withdraw` already make, and `lib/cashback/paths.ts` documents
it: a retailer whose slug is `join` becomes unreachable rather than shadowing
the page. `join` is chosen over `opt-in` partly because a hyphen is a legal
merchant slug and a bare word is less likely to collide.

**Naming to keep apart:** `t.seeTerms` in the cashback catalogue is the
*retailer's* own conditions. This page is the *programme's* terms. Neither
string should drift into the other's job.

# F3 — the terms, and the opt-in

## Context

A member can now sign up, sign in and become an account (#565, #569), and no
cashback page renders for a stranger (#573). **They cannot opt in**, so they
cannot click out — the backend landed B3 (#568) while this work was going on,
and `POST /clickouts` now answers **403** to anybody without a participation.
`api.optIn()` has existed with zero call sites since it was written.

So F3 is the last frontend blocker on the path to one real transaction:
sign up → **opt in** → click out → a pending entry.

Two PRs. The founder settled the open question earlier: **I draft the terms as
a statement of what the code enforces**, each clause traceable to a mechanism,
with the PR saying plainly that counsel-approved text replaces it before
launch.

### Done since the last plan (not repeated below)

`.mcp.json` carries both servers (#582, merged). The stale-issue sweep is
finished: 143 open → 99, nineteen closed with commit evidence, five left open
deliberately with the reasons recorded on #206 and #275. Both are off this
plan.

---

## Route decisions

**`/{lang}/terms`** — free; `/{lang}/` currently holds `about`, `contact`,
`faq`, `impressum`, `legal`, `privacy`, `register`, `setup`, `signin`.

**`/{lang}/{place}/cashback/join`** for the opt-in. A static segment beside
`[slug].astro`, which Astro resolves before the dynamic one — the same trade
`wallet` and `withdraw` already make, and `lib/cashback/paths.ts` documents
it: a retailer whose slug is `join` becomes unreachable rather than shadowing
the page. `join` is chosen over `opt-in` partly because a hyphen is a legal
merchant slug and a bare word is less likely to collide.

**Naming to keep apart:** `t.seeTerms` in the cashback catalogue is the
*retailer's* own conditions. This page is the *programme's* terms. Neither
string should drift into the other's job.

## The states the opt-in screen must answer

Not one state, five, and the second is the one that is easy to miss:

| `GET /participation` | Means | Screen |
|---|---|---|
| **404** | never opted in | the opt-in, with the terms |
| **200 `status: "left"`** | opted in once, left since | the same screen — the upsert re-joins, and `queries/participation.sql` says so: *"left → active re-states opted_in_at, terms_version"* |
| 200 `status: "active"` | already in | send them on to the wallet; nothing to accept |
| **503** | the deployment names no brand (`ErrNoBrand`) | say so, and do not retry — no version exists to accept |
| 401 | not a member the api knows | the fence and #573's band already own this |

And on the POST: **409** already active (a double submit — treat as success and
move on), **400** the version moved under them (reload rather than re-post a
stale consent — a stale consent is never recorded, by design).

## Where the terms are reachable from

The opt-in screen, and the wallet's participation area. **Not the site
footer** — that carries the three notices a German-facing service legally owes
(`SiteFooter.astro:88-94`), and these are programme terms. A member who has
accepted them still has to be able to find them again, and with no settings
page the wallet is the only honest home.

*(implementation detail pending survey results)*

---

## PR 1 — `/{lang}/terms`

**`web/src/lib/legal/terms.ts`**, beside `legal/strings.ts`. Shaped on
`lib/faq/strings.ts`, which is the repository's existing *prose* catalogue
(`sections → entries → answer: readonly string[]`) rather than
`legal/strings.ts`, which is term/value pairs. Terms wants
`clauses: readonly { heading, body: readonly string[] }[]`, plus the page's
own heading, intro, and the sentence that cites the version.

It also exports the version the text was written against, for the drift check
above.

**`web/src/pages/[lang]/terms.astro`** — the single-pane legal-family page,
copying `impressum.astro`'s frontmatter exactly: the `isReadingLanguage`
guard rewriting to `/404`, `brandOnHand({ brandDir: BRAND_DIR, appEnv: APP_ENV })`,
the `Masthead` language switcher linking `/el/terms` ↔ `/de/terms`, and
`ReaderLayout`. **Not** a fourth `LegalPane`: that component renders
term/value pairs out of `brand.legal` and a `note` block, and prose would
distort it.

It reuses `LegalPane`'s precedent for saying where the content came from —
`source === BRAND_SOURCE_FIXTURE` gets the same kind of note the imprint gets
(`LegalPane.astro:80-87`).

**The clauses**, each one a rule the code enforces. Written from the survey's
citations, and any clause the survey cannot substantiate is dropped rather
than softened.

## PR 2 — the opt-in

**`web/src/pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/join.astro`**, plus a
`joinPath(lang, slugs)` helper in `lib/cashback/paths.ts` beside
`walletPath`/`withdrawPath`.

Frontmatter follows the four sibling cashback pages: `parseAxes`, the session
from `sessionOf`, `createCashbackApi`, and the `isUnauthorized` branch #573
added. It reads `GET /participation` and renders per the state table above.

The POST is guarded by `isSameOrigin` (`lib/csrf.ts`) as every other
state-changing form here is, and posts `brand.legal.documents.terms.version`
through the existing `api.optIn(version)` — which has been waiting for a
caller since it was written.

Copy: `t.notParticipating` and `t.optIn` already exist in both languages and
are reused; the new strings are the acceptance sentence, the version line, the
no-brand refusal and the drift refusal.

**`wallet.astro`**: the not-participating band stops linking to the catalogue
(`cataloguePath`) and links here.

## Verification

Per PR, the gates that already exist:

```sh
cd web && npm run check && npm test && npm run build
sh scripts/lint-brand-literals.sh        # on a clean worktree
sh scripts/lint-refs.sh "$(git branch --show-current)"
sh scripts/lint-refs.sh --from-messages origin/main..HEAD
sh scripts/lint-commit-authors.sh origin/main..HEAD
```

Rendered-page tests on the `wallet.test.ts` pattern (container + fixtures +
string assertions), including — learning from #583 — **a case with a session
filed by hand via `rememberSession`**, because the container runs no
middleware and every branch behind a session is otherwise untested.

Then, since previews are down, on QA after merge: sign in, land on the
wallet, follow the band to the opt-in, accept, and confirm the wallet stops
offering it. The terms page is checkable signed-out in both languages
immediately.

Two carried notes: `src/lib/astro-url-scheme.test.ts` times out under
full-suite load on this machine and passes with `--testTimeout=30000` (#132,
not ours); and every new logic module must join `web/vitest.config.ts`'s
coverage `include` or it escapes the 80% gate silently.

*(clause citations pending the second survey)*

### `web/src/pages/[lang]/faq.astro` — frontmatter verbatim (lines 1–36)

```astro
---
import { APP_ENV, BRAND_DIR } from 'astro:env/server';

import Masthead from '../../components/Masthead.astro';
import ReaderLayout from '../../layouts/ReaderLayout.astro';
import { brandOnHand } from '../../lib/brand/load';
import { faqStrings } from '../../lib/faq/strings';
import { frontPagePath, isReadingLanguage } from '../../lib/reader/axes';

// The FAQ (issue #528). Its own rule, printed on its own face: the answers
// are the same sentences the screens already say, and if this page said
// something different, one of the two would be wrong. So lib/faq/strings.ts
// owns the questions and holds no answer — every answer is a reference into
// a catalogue that already renders it elsewhere.
//
// Not a member surface, so no MemberBar: this route carries a language axis
// and no place axis, and MemberBar's links are all place-scoped. Building
// one here would mean choosing a place on the reader's behalf, which is the
// one thing Principle VII forbids.
//
// No accordion and no client script. Every answer is open, as the board
// draws it — a disclosure widget would hide eight short answers behind
// eight clicks and take a keyboard user through all of them to read one.
const langSegment = Astro.params['lang'];
if (langSegment === undefined || !isReadingLanguage(langSegment)) {
  return Astro.rewrite('/404');
}
const lang = langSegment;
const t = faqStrings(lang);
const { brand } = brandOnHand({ brandDir: BRAND_DIR, appEnv: APP_ENV });

// The page has a language axis but no place axis, so the brand falls back to
// the flagship places under the READER'S language. DEFAULT_FRONT_PAGE is
// hard-coded to Greek and would flip a German reader's language axis (FR-009).
const home = frontPagePath(lang, ['munich', 'greece']);
---
```

### `web/src/lib/cashback/paths.ts` — complete (56 lines)

```ts
import type { ReadingLanguage } from '../reader/axes';

/**
 * The cashback URL scheme, built in one place.
 *
 * `/{lang}/{place[+place…]}/cashback/…` — the same two axes the reader
 * pages carry, in the same two segments, for the reason Principle VII
 * gives: a Greek speaker in Munich reads Greek about Munich, and the two
 * facts travel separately. The catalogue endpoint takes `lang` and `place`
 * as separate parameters, so the URL that leads to it does too.
 *
 * `wallet` and `withdraw` are static segments under the same prefix a
 * merchant slug occupies. Astro resolves a static route before a dynamic
 * one, so `/el/munich/cashback/wallet` reaches the wallet even if a
 * retailer is ever slugged `wallet` — and that retailer becomes
 * unreachable rather than the wallet becoming a shop, which is the right
 * way round for the failure to fall.
 */

/** The place segment: slugs joined the way the reader pages join them. */
export function placeSegment(slugs: readonly string[]): string {
  return slugs.join('+');
}

/** The catalogue — the cashback front door. */
export function cataloguePath(lang: ReadingLanguage, slugs: readonly string[]): string {
  return `/${lang}/${placeSegment(slugs)}/cashback`;
}

/** The member's wallet and entry list. */
export function walletPath(lang: ReadingLanguage, slugs: readonly string[]): string {
  return `${cataloguePath(lang, slugs)}/wallet`;
}

/** The withdrawal request and its status. */
export function withdrawPath(lang: ReadingLanguage, slugs: readonly string[]): string {
  return `${cataloguePath(lang, slugs)}/withdraw`;
}

/** One retailer's page. */
export function merchantPath(
  lang: ReadingLanguage,
  slugs: readonly string[],
  merchantSlug: string,
): string {
  return `${cataloguePath(lang, slugs)}/${encodeURIComponent(merchantSlug)}`;
}

/** The operator queues, which carry no axes: an operator works in one place. */
export const OPS_PATHS = {
  unattributed: '/ops/unattributed',
  held: '/ops/held',
  withdrawals: '/ops/withdrawals',
  reconciliation: '/ops/reconciliation',
} as const;
```

### `web/src/lib/cashback/paths.ts` — complete (56 lines)

```ts
import type { ReadingLanguage } from '../reader/axes';

/**
 * The cashback URL scheme, built in one place.
 *
 * `/{lang}/{place[+place…]}/cashback/…` — the same two axes the reader
 * pages carry, in the same two segments, for the reason Principle VII
 * gives: a Greek speaker in Munich reads Greek about Munich, and the two
 * facts travel separately. The catalogue endpoint takes `lang` and `place`
 * as separate parameters, so the URL that leads to it does too.
 *
 * `wallet` and `withdraw` are static segments under the same prefix a
 * merchant slug occupies. Astro resolves a static route before a dynamic
 * one, so `/el/munich/cashback/wallet` reaches the wallet even if a
 * retailer is ever slugged `wallet` — and that retailer becomes
 * unreachable rather than the wallet becoming a shop, which is the right
 * way round for the failure to fall.
 */

/** The place segment: slugs joined the way the reader pages join them. */
export function placeSegment(slugs: readonly string[]): string {
  return slugs.join('+');
}

/** The catalogue — the cashback front door. */
export function cataloguePath(lang: ReadingLanguage, slugs: readonly string[]): string {
  return `/${lang}/${placeSegment(slugs)}/cashback`;
}

/** The member's wallet and entry list. */
export function walletPath(lang: ReadingLanguage, slugs: readonly string[]): string {
  return `${cataloguePath(lang, slugs)}/wallet`;
}

/** The withdrawal request and its status. */
export function withdrawPath(lang: ReadingLanguage, slugs: readonly string[]): string {
  return `${cataloguePath(lang, slugs)}/withdraw`;
}

/** One retailer's page. */
export function merchantPath(
  lang: ReadingLanguage,
  slugs: readonly string[],
  merchantSlug: string,
): string {
  return `${cataloguePath(lang, slugs)}/${encodeURIComponent(merchantSlug)}`;
}

/** The operator queues, which carry no axes: an operator works in one place. */
export const OPS_PATHS = {
  unattributed: '/ops/unattributed',
  held: '/ops/held',
  withdrawals: '/ops/withdrawals',
  reconciliation: '/ops/reconciliation',
} as const;
```

The style to match for a new helper: a one-line `/** … */`, `(lang: ReadingLanguage, slugs: readonly string[]): string`, body a template literal over `cataloguePath(lang, slugs)`. Insert after `withdrawPath` and before `merchantPath` — and note the docstring's static-vs-dynamic-segment argument already justifies a new static segment, but the docstring names `wallet` and `withdraw` explicitly, so it wants updating.

**Middleware consequence, free of charge:** a route at `/{lang}/{place}/cashback/opt-in` is automatically behind the member fence — `isCashbackPath` at `web/src/middleware.ts:159-165` matches `/^\/[^/]+\/[^/]+\/cashback(?:\/|$)/`, and `needsSignIn(authenticated, fixtures)` (`web/src/lib/member/gate.ts:23-25`) is `!fixtures && !authenticated`. `gate.ts:12` says it outright: *"A fifth page added later is gated by existing."* Fixture mode is exempt, so previews still render.

If the terms page instead lives at `/{lang}/terms` it is **not** fenced (`isCashbackPath` needs two segments before `cashback`) — which is what you want for a legal document.

## 7. i18n rules a new module must satisfy

`web/src/i18n/cashback.test.ts` (132 lines). Its assertions, quoted:

```ts
  it('carries the same keys in every language, to the same depth', () => {
    const shape = (value: unknown): unknown => {
      if (typeof value === 'function') {
        return 'fn';
      }
      if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null) {
        return typeof value;
      }
      return Object.fromEntries(
        Object.entries(value as Record<string, unknown>)
          .map(([key, nested]) => [key, shape(nested)] as const)
          .sort(([a], [b]) => a.localeCompare(b)),
      );
    };
    const [first, ...rest] = READING_LANGUAGES.map((lang) => shape(cashbackStrings(lang)));
    for (const other of rest) {
      expect(other).toEqual(first);
    }
```

### `web/src/lib/cashback/paths.ts` — complete (56 lines)

```ts
import type { ReadingLanguage } from '../reader/axes';

/**
 * The cashback URL scheme, built in one place.
 *
 * `/{lang}/{place[+place…]}/cashback/…` — the same two axes the reader
 * pages carry, in the same two segments, for the reason Principle VII
 * gives: a Greek speaker in Munich reads Greek about Munich, and the two
 * facts travel separately. The catalogue endpoint takes `lang` and `place`
 * as separate parameters, so the URL that leads to it does too.
 *
 * `wallet` and `withdraw` are static segments under the same prefix a
 * merchant slug occupies. Astro resolves a static route before a dynamic
 * one, so `/el/munich/cashback/wallet` reaches the wallet even if a
 * retailer is ever slugged `wallet` — and that retailer becomes
 * unreachable rather than the wallet becoming a shop, which is the right
 * way round for the failure to fall.
 */

/** The place segment: slugs joined the way the reader pages join them. */
export function placeSegment(slugs: readonly string[]): string {
  return slugs.join('+');
}

/** The catalogue — the cashback front door. */
export function cataloguePath(lang: ReadingLanguage, slugs: readonly string[]): string {
  return `/${lang}/${placeSegment(slugs)}/cashback`;
}

/** The member's wallet and entry list. */
export function walletPath(lang: ReadingLanguage, slugs: readonly string[]): string {
  return `${cataloguePath(lang, slugs)}/wallet`;
}

/** The withdrawal request and its status. */
export function withdrawPath(lang: ReadingLanguage, slugs: readonly string[]): string {
  return `${cataloguePath(lang, slugs)}/withdraw`;
}

/** One retailer's page. */
export function merchantPath(
  lang: ReadingLanguage,
  slugs: readonly string[],
  merchantSlug: string,
): string {
  return `${cataloguePath(lang, slugs)}/${encodeURIComponent(merchantSlug)}`;
}

/** The operator queues, which carry no axes: an operator works in one place. */
export const OPS_PATHS = {
  unattributed: '/ops/unattributed',
  held: '/ops/held',
  withdrawals: '/ops/withdrawals',
  reconciliation: '/ops/reconciliation',
} as const;
```

The style to match for a new helper: a one-line `/** … */`, `(lang: ReadingLanguage, slugs: readonly string[]): string`, body a template literal over `cataloguePath(lang, slugs)`. Insert after `withdrawPath` and before `merchantPath` — and note the docstring's static-vs-dynamic-segment argument already justifies a new static segment, but the docstring names `wallet` and `withdraw` explicitly, so it wants updating.

**Middleware consequence, free of charge:** a route at `/{lang}/{place}/cashback/opt-in` is automatically behind the member fence — `isCashbackPath` at `web/src/middleware.ts:159-165` matches `/^\/[^/]+\/[^/]+\/cashback(?:\/|$)/`, and `needsSignIn(authenticated, fixtures)` (`web/src/lib/member/gate.ts:23-25`) is `!fixtures && !authenticated`. `gate.ts:12` says it outright: *"A fifth page added later is gated by existing."* Fixture mode is exempt, so previews still render.

If the terms page instead lives at `/{lang}/terms` it is **not** fenced (`isCashbackPath` needs two segments before `cashback`) — which is what you want for a legal document.
