# F3 — the terms, and the opt-in

## Context

A member can now sign up, sign in and become an account (#565, #569), and no
cashback page renders for a stranger (#573). **They cannot opt in**, so they
cannot click out — the backend landed B3 (#568) while this work was going on,
and `POST /clickouts` now answers **403** to anybody without a participation.
`api.optIn()` has existed with zero call sites since it was written.

So F3 is the last frontend blocker on the path to one real transaction:
sign up → **opt in** → click out → a pending entry.

Two PRs. The founder settled the open question earlier: **I draft the terms as
a statement of what the code enforces**, each clause traceable to a mechanism,
with the PR saying plainly that counsel-approved text replaces it before
launch.

### Done since the last plan (not repeated below)

`.mcp.json` carries both servers (#582, merged). The stale-issue sweep is
finished: 143 open → 99, nineteen closed with commit evidence, five left open
deliberately with the reasons recorded on #206 and #275. Both are off this
plan.

---

## Route decisions

**`/{lang}/terms`** — free; `/{lang}/` currently holds `about`, `contact`,
`faq`, `impressum`, `legal`, `privacy`, `register`, `setup`, `signin`.

**`/{lang}/{place}/cashback/join`** for the opt-in. A static segment beside
`[slug].astro`, which Astro resolves before the dynamic one — the same trade
`wallet` and `withdraw` already make, and `lib/cashback/paths.ts` documents
it: a retailer whose slug is `join` becomes unreachable rather than shadowing
the page. `join` is chosen over `opt-in` partly because a hyphen is a legal
merchant slug and a bare word is less likely to collide.

**Naming to keep apart:** `t.seeTerms` in the cashback catalogue is the
*retailer's* own conditions. This page is the *programme's* terms. Neither
string should drift into the other's job.

## The states the opt-in screen must answer

Not one state, five, and the second is the one that is easy to miss:

| `GET /participation` | Means | Screen |
|---|---|---|
| **404** | never opted in | the opt-in, with the terms |
| **200 `status: "left"`** | opted in once, left since | the same screen — the upsert re-joins, and `queries/participation.sql` says so: *"left → active re-states opted_in_at, terms_version"* |
| 200 `status: "active"` | already in | send them on to the wallet; nothing to accept |
| **503** | the deployment names no brand (`ErrNoBrand`) | say so, and do not retry — no version exists to accept |
| 401 | not a member the api knows | the fence and #573's band already own this |

And on the POST: **409** already active (a double submit — treat as success and
move on), **400** the version moved under them (reload rather than re-post a
stale consent — a stale consent is never recorded, by design).

## Where the terms are reachable from

The opt-in screen, and the wallet's participation area. **Not the site
footer** — that carries the three notices a German-facing service legally owes
(`SiteFooter.astro:88-94`), and these are programme terms. A member who has
accepted them still has to be able to find them again, and with no settings
page the wallet is the only honest home.

## The version/text drift, and what to do about it

Checked, and it shapes the design: **the brand carries no terms text.**
`Document` is `{ id, version }` and nothing else
(`web/src/lib/brand/brand.types.ts:33-36`), and a brand directory holds one
`brand.json` with no document beside it. So the *version* comes from the
deployment and the *text* comes from a copy module in this repository, and the
two can drift the moment somebody bumps `3.1.0` to `3.2.0`.

Left alone, that means a member reads text written for one version and accepts
another — which is precisely the failure `POST /participation` refusing a
stale `terms_version` exists to prevent, reintroduced one layer up.

So the copy module **declares the version it was written against**, and the
page compares:

- versions agree → the terms render, the opt-in offers acceptance;
- versions differ → the page says so plainly and **does not offer the button**.

That is the same posture the brief already demands for `ErrNoBrand` — *"the
page says so rather than retrying"* — and the same principle as the api's own
refusal: consent is not collected against text this deployment cannot vouch
for. A version bump then costs somebody a deliberate edit to the copy, which
is the point.

---

## PR 1 — `/{lang}/terms`

**`web/src/lib/legal/terms.ts`**, beside `legal/strings.ts`. Shaped on
`lib/faq/strings.ts`, which is the repository's existing *prose* catalogue
(`sections → entries → answer: readonly string[]`) rather than
`legal/strings.ts`, which is term/value pairs. Terms wants
`clauses: readonly { heading, body: readonly string[] }[]`, plus the page's
own heading, intro, and the sentence that cites the version.

It also exports the version the text was written against, for the drift check
above.

**`web/src/pages/[lang]/terms.astro`** — the single-pane legal-family page,
copying `impressum.astro`'s frontmatter exactly: the `isReadingLanguage`
guard rewriting to `/404`, `brandOnHand({ brandDir: BRAND_DIR, appEnv: APP_ENV })`,
the `Masthead` language switcher linking `/el/terms` ↔ `/de/terms`, and
`ReaderLayout`. **Not** a fourth `LegalPane`: that component renders
term/value pairs out of `brand.legal` and a `note` block, and prose would
distort it.

It reuses `LegalPane`'s precedent for saying where the content came from —
`source === BRAND_SOURCE_FIXTURE` gets the same kind of note the imprint gets
(`LegalPane.astro:80-87`).

**The clauses**, each one a rule the code enforces. Written from the survey's
citations, and any clause the survey cannot substantiate is dropped rather
than softened.

## PR 2 — the opt-in

**`web/src/pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/join.astro`**, plus a
`joinPath(lang, slugs)` helper in `lib/cashback/paths.ts` beside
`walletPath`/`withdrawPath`.

Frontmatter follows the four sibling cashback pages: `parseAxes`, the session
from `sessionOf`, `createCashbackApi`, and the `isUnauthorized` branch #573
added. It reads `GET /participation` and renders per the state table above.

The POST is guarded by `isSameOrigin` (`lib/csrf.ts`) as every other
state-changing form here is, and posts `brand.legal.documents.terms.version`
through the existing `api.optIn(version)` — which has been waiting for a
caller since it was written.

Copy: `t.notParticipating` and `t.optIn` already exist in both languages and
are reused; the new strings are the acceptance sentence, the version line, the
no-brand refusal and the drift refusal.

**`wallet.astro`**: the not-participating band stops linking to the catalogue
(`cataloguePath`) and links here.

## Verification

Per PR, the gates that already exist:

```sh
cd web && npm run check && npm test && npm run build
sh scripts/lint-brand-literals.sh        # on a clean worktree
sh scripts/lint-refs.sh "$(git branch --show-current)"
sh scripts/lint-refs.sh --from-messages origin/main..HEAD
sh scripts/lint-commit-authors.sh origin/main..HEAD
```

Rendered-page tests on the `wallet.test.ts` pattern (container + fixtures +
string assertions), including — learning from #583 — **a case with a session
filed by hand via `rememberSession`**, because the container runs no
middleware and every branch behind a session is otherwise untested.

Then, since previews are down, on QA after merge: sign in, land on the
wallet, follow the band to the opt-in, accept, and confirm the wallet stops
offering it. The terms page is checkable signed-out in both languages
immediately.

Two carried notes: `src/lib/astro-url-scheme.test.ts` times out under
full-suite load on this machine and passes with `--testTimeout=30000` (#132,
not ours); and every new logic module must join `web/vitest.config.ts`'s
coverage `include` or it escapes the 80% gate silently.

*(clause citations pending the second survey)*

# F3 — the terms, and the opt-in

## Context

A member can now sign up, sign in and become an account (#565, #569), and no
cashback page renders for a stranger (#573). **They cannot opt in**, so they
cannot click out — the backend landed B3 (#568) while this work was going on,
and `POST /clickouts` now answers **403** to anybody without a participation.
`api.optIn()` has existed with zero call sites since it was written.

So F3 is the last frontend blocker on the path to one real transaction:
sign up → **opt in** → click out → a pending entry.

Two PRs. The founder settled the open question earlier: **I draft the terms as
a statement of what the code enforces**, each clause traceable to a mechanism,
with the PR saying plainly that counsel-approved text replaces it before
launch.

### Done since the last plan (not repeated below)

`.mcp.json` carries both servers (#582, merged). The stale-issue sweep is
finished: 143 open → 99, nineteen closed with commit evidence, five left open
deliberately with the reasons recorded on #206 and #275. Both are off this
plan.

---

## Route decisions

**`/{lang}/terms`** — free; `/{lang}/` currently holds `about`, `contact`,
`faq`, `impressum`, `legal`, `privacy`, `register`, `setup`, `signin`.

**`/{lang}/{place}/cashback/join`** for the opt-in. A static segment beside
`[slug].astro`, which Astro resolves before the dynamic one — the same trade
`wallet` and `withdraw` already make, and `lib/cashback/paths.ts` documents
it: a retailer whose slug is `join` becomes unreachable rather than shadowing
the page. `join` is chosen over `opt-in` partly because a hyphen is a legal
merchant slug and a bare word is less likely to collide.

**Naming to keep apart:** `t.seeTerms` in the cashback catalogue is the
*retailer's* own conditions. This page is the *programme's* terms. Neither
string should drift into the other's job.

## The states the opt-in screen must answer

Not one state, five, and the second is the one that is easy to miss:

| `GET /participation` | Means | Screen |
|---|---|---|
| **404** | never opted in | the opt-in, with the terms |
| **200 `status: "left"`** | opted in once, left since | the same screen — the upsert re-joins, and `queries/participation.sql` says so: *"left → active re-states opted_in_at, terms_version"* |
| 200 `status: "active"` | already in | send them on to the wallet; nothing to accept |
| **503** | the deployment names no brand (`ErrNoBrand`) | say so, and do not retry — no version exists to accept |
| 401 | not a member the api knows | the fence and #573's band already own this |

And on the POST: **409** already active (a double submit — treat as success and
move on), **400** the version moved under them (reload rather than re-post a
stale consent — a stale consent is never recorded, by design).

## Where the terms are reachable from

The opt-in screen, and the wallet's participation area. **Not the site
footer** — that carries the three notices a German-facing service legally owes
(`SiteFooter.astro:88-94`), and these are programme terms. A member who has
accepted them still has to be able to find them again, and with no settings
page the wallet is the only honest home.

## The version/text drift, and what to do about it

Checked, and it shapes the design: **the brand carries no terms text.**
`Document` is `{ id, version }` and nothing else
(`web/src/lib/brand/brand.types.ts:33-36`), and a brand directory holds one
`brand.json` with no document beside it. So the *version* comes from the
deployment and the *text* comes from a copy module in this repository, and the
two can drift the moment somebody bumps `3.1.0` to `3.2.0`.

Left alone, that means a member reads text written for one version and accepts
another — which is precisely the failure `POST /participation` refusing a
stale `terms_version` exists to prevent, reintroduced one layer up.

So the copy module **declares the version it was written against**, and the
page compares:

- versions agree → the terms render, the opt-in offers acceptance;
- versions differ → the page says so plainly and **does not offer the button**.

That is the same posture the brief already demands for `ErrNoBrand` — *"the
page says so rather than retrying"* — and the same principle as the api's own
refusal: consent is not collected against text this deployment cannot vouch
for. A version bump then costs somebody a deliberate edit to the copy, which
is the point.

---

## PR 1 — `/{lang}/terms`

**`web/src/lib/legal/terms.ts`**, beside `legal/strings.ts`. Shaped on
`lib/faq/strings.ts`, which is the repository's existing *prose* catalogue
(`sections → entries → answer: readonly string[]`) rather than
`legal/strings.ts`, which is term/value pairs. Terms wants
`clauses: readonly { heading, body: readonly string[] }[]`, plus the page's
own heading, intro, and the sentence that cites the version.

It also exports the version the text was written against, for the drift check
above.

**`web/src/pages/[lang]/terms.astro`** — the single-pane legal-family page,
copying `impressum.astro`'s frontmatter exactly: the `isReadingLanguage`
guard rewriting to `/404`, `brandOnHand({ brandDir: BRAND_DIR, appEnv: APP_ENV })`,
the `Masthead` language switcher linking `/el/terms` ↔ `/de/terms`, and
`ReaderLayout`. **Not** a fourth `LegalPane`: that component renders
term/value pairs out of `brand.legal` and a `note` block, and prose would
distort it.

It reuses `LegalPane`'s precedent for saying where the content came from —
`source === BRAND_SOURCE_FIXTURE` gets the same kind of note the imprint gets
(`LegalPane.astro:80-87`).

**The clauses**, each one a rule the code enforces. Written from the survey's
citations, and any clause the survey cannot substantiate is dropped rather
than softened.

## PR 2 — the opt-in

**`web/src/pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/join.astro`**, plus a
`joinPath(lang, slugs)` helper in `lib/cashback/paths.ts` beside
`walletPath`/`withdrawPath`.

Frontmatter follows the four sibling cashback pages: `parseAxes`, the session
from `sessionOf`, `createCashbackApi`, and the `isUnauthorized` branch #573
added. It reads `GET /participation` and renders per the state table above.

The POST is guarded by `isSameOrigin` (`lib/csrf.ts`) as every other
state-changing form here is, and posts `brand.legal.documents.terms.version`
through the existing `api.optIn(version)` — which has been waiting for a
caller since it was written.

Copy: `t.notParticipating` and `t.optIn` already exist in both languages and
are reused; the new strings are the acceptance sentence, the version line, the
no-brand refusal and the drift refusal.

**`wallet.astro`**: the not-participating band stops linking to the catalogue
(`cataloguePath`) and links here.

## Verification

Per PR, the gates that already exist:

```sh
cd web && npm run check && npm test && npm run build
sh scripts/lint-brand-literals.sh        # on a clean worktree
sh scripts/lint-refs.sh "$(git branch --show-current)"
sh scripts/lint-refs.sh --from-messages origin/main..HEAD
sh scripts/lint-commit-authors.sh origin/main..HEAD
```

Rendered-page tests on the `wallet.test.ts` pattern (container + fixtures +
string assertions), including — learning from #583 — **a case with a session
filed by hand via `rememberSession`**, because the container runs no
middleware and every branch behind a session is otherwise untested.

Then, since previews are down, on QA after merge: sign in, land on the
wallet, follow the band to the opt-in, accept, and confirm the wallet stops
offering it. The terms page is checkable signed-out in both languages
immediately.

Two carried notes: `src/lib/astro-url-scheme.test.ts` times out under
full-suite load on this machine and passes with `--testTimeout=30000` (#132,
not ours); and every new logic module must join `web/vitest.config.ts`'s
coverage `include` or it escapes the 80% gate silently.

---

**1. In fixture mode the opt-in screen is invisible.** `api.ts:177-184`'s
fixture `participation()` returns `status: 'active'`, so the wallet always
shows a participating member and the not-participating band never draws — on
every preview and every `make cashback-demo`. Changing the fixture to return
`null` would fix that and break the wallet's own preview, which is worse.

`api.source === 'fixture'`**, above the usual `FixtureNotice`. A reviewer
reaches it by URL and sees the real screen; nothing is recorded, because the
fixture client resolves without writing.

where to read it, never what it is.**

## 1. Click-time rate governs the credit — **TRUE, strongly enforced**

**Snapshot written** at `C:\Users\madym\repos\apivo-news\internal\cashback\clickout\click.go:241-256` — `Clicks.Record` marshals the whole rate band to JSON and writes it beside the share:

**Read back** at `C:\Users\madym\repos\apivo-news\internal\cashback\clickout\click.go:312-345` (`clickFrom`), which unmarshals `row.RateSnapshot` into a `catalogue.RateBand` and rebuilds `Promised: Promise{Rate: band, MemberShare: share}`.

**Applied when the entry is opened** at `C:\Users\madym\repos\apivo-news\internal\cashback\earnings\lifecycle.go:295` — `share, err := ShareOf(commission, click.Promised)` — and the policy is spelled out at `C:\Users\madym\repos\apivo-news\internal\cashback\earnings\share.go:66-79`:

> The rate comes from the CLICK, never from the offer as it stands now (FR-013). A member who clicked a published band is owed that band even if it has since been withdrawn, lowered, or the retailer has left the network.

The click row is **append-only**: trigger `click_immutable` at `C:\Users\madym\repos\apivo-news\internal\platform\db\migrations\0012_cashback_clicks_evidence.up.sql:73-78` runs `public.raise_immutable()` on update/delete/truncate, so the snapshot cannot be rewritten. Column comment (`internal/cashback/*/store/models.go:93-96`): *"This, not the offer row as it stands today, is what governs the credit - a rate change after the click never reaches back."*

There is a dedicated end-to-end test: `TestTheClickTimeRateGovernsTheCredit`, `C:\Users\madym\repos\apivo-news\internal\cashback\earnings\journey_integration_test.go:405-539` (publishes a new rate mid-journey and asserts the old share is credited).

**One nuance you should NOT overstate:** the *rate* is snapshotted; the *commission* is whatever the network actually reported. `share.go:75-78`: *"The commission is what the network ACTUALLY reported, not what the band predicted. Those differ routinely — a partial refund, a currency the network settled at a different rate, a correction."* So "the rate that applied is the rate that governs" is true; "the amount you saw is the amount you get" is **not**.

**Bonus member-favourable fact you can state:** rounding always goes the member's way — `MemberFavour = money.RoundCeil`, `C:\Users\madym\repos\apivo-news\internal\cashback\earnings\share.go:27`, with the sub-unit difference absorbed by the house (`Share.Rounding`, lines 53-63).

## 2. States and transitions — **TRUE, six states, table is explicit**

`C:\Users\madym\repos\apivo-news\internal\cashback\earnings\state.go:23-41` defines exactly six: `held`, `pending`, `confirmed`, `reserved`, `paid`, `reversed`.

The transition table, `state.go:85-92`:

```go
	StateHeld:      {StatePending},
	StatePending:   {StateHeld, StateConfirmed},
	StateConfirmed: {StateReserved},
```

```sql
state text not null
    constraint entry_state_known

```

Same six on the history table (`from_state`/`to_state`, lines 214-220), plus `check (from_state is null or from_state <> to_state)` at line 234.

Terminality is a trigger, `0013:129-131`:
```sql
if old.state in ('paid', 'reversed') and new.state is distinct from old.state then
    raise exception 'cashback entry state % is terminal: a paid or reversed entry never becomes payable again', old.state;
```

**Spendable:** only `confirmed`. `state.go:30-32`: *"the only state that counts toward the withdrawal threshold (FR-043)."* Enforced at `C:\Users\madym\repos\apivo-news\internal\cashback\payout\withdrawal.go:241-247` — the withdrawal reserves from `machine.Confirmed(...)` and `reachesTheThreshold` sums only those rows.

Commits `5814b8f`, `0cdcdb1`, `a4aae3e`, migration `0036_entry_currency_is_the_members`. Three layers:

### (f) A click carries its network — **#579, mostly invisible to members but it fixes a real hazard**

Migration `C:\Users\madym\repos\apivo-news\internal\platform\db\migrations\0037_click_carries_its_network.up.sql`, commits `9818414`, `cb07c3f`, `61f61b0`. The click now stores `merchant_network_id` and `network_id`, pinned by two composite FKs (`click_route_matches_offer`, `click_network_matches_route`, lines 61-66) so they cannot disagree with the offer.

`lifecycle.go:316-329` — a second report citing an already-credited click is **queued for an operator, not credited twice**. Same for a reference nobody minted (FR-034 unattributed queue). ### (h) Payouts are made oldest-first
`C:\Users\madym\repos\apivo-news\internal\cashback\earnings\queries\entry.sql:103-105`: *"cashback is paid out in the order it was earned, so a member's oldest confirmed money leaves first and nothing can sit at the back of the queue indefinitely."* Nice thing to promise.

`0014:139-140`: `check (state <> 'rejected' or (decision_reason is not null and btrim(decision_reason) <> ''))` — *"A refusal that records no reason is a refusal the member cannot be told about and an operator cannot be held to."* Reserved money returns to `confirmed` on rejection (`state.go:78-81`).

`withdrawal.go:211-218` and `0014:115-121` — the money moves `confirmed → reserved` **before** any human reviews it. So the member's spendable balance drops at request time, not approval time. Worth saying, or they'll think money vanished.

### (k) Credits can be slow by design
`C:\Users\madym\repos\apivo-news\internal\platform\db\migrations\0033_network_reporting_lag_minutes.up.sql` — each network declares how far behind the present it reports; the sweep won't ask for data the network doesn't have yet. `GET /api/v1/cashback/export` is in the wallet route table (`wallet/handlers.go:99`). Worth a line if your terms page covers data rights.

`lib/faq/strings.ts` set the precedent — it owns questions and no answers, so the FAQ cannot become a second source of truth. F3a is up as **[#590](https://github.com/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/pull/590)** (closes #589). Starting the opt-in screen now, but two things from the build are worth your attention first.

## A clause I wrote, then deleted

I'd assumed a click stops being creditable after some window, and drafted a clause saying so. **It doesn't exist.** `Matcher.Match` matches on `(network, click_ref)` with no time predicate at all — offers expire and networks have query windows, but attribution has no bound. A terms page is the wrong place to invent one, so it's gone rather than softened.

Same category, caught before it shipped: the clause says the **rate** at click governs, not the amount. The commission is whatever the network actually reports, and those differ routinely — a partial refund, a currency settled differently. "The rate you saw applies" is true; "the amount you saw is what you get" would have been a lie.

## A disclosure gap the terms now close

`Totals.Held` is **deliberately excluded** from `GET /wallet`. So a held credit appears in your entry list marked held, and in **no balance anywhere** — the money is real, the network reported it, and a named operator has to release it. Nothing told a member that. The terms page now does, and it's the only place that does.

Worth deciding separately whether the wallet should surface it too. I've left that alone rather than widen this PR.

## How the terms are built

The clauses are the product's own sentences, pulled from `i18n/cashback.ts` — the same discipline `lib/faq/strings.ts` uses so the FAQ can't become a second source of truth. The module owns **13 headings** and exactly **7 statements**, and a test counts them, so an eighth has to be a deliberate edit rather than a slow slide back into writing our own copy.

Each of the seven is checked against the code: holds, never-clawed-back-after-payout (`state.go` — a reversal after payout is the house's loss), the minimum, the single currency (#577's migration), claim-not-stored-value (FR-041, verified *negatively* — there is no transfer, gift, spend or top-up route anywhere), leaving-deletes-nothing (migration 0017 refuses `DELETE` outright), and minor units.

## The version check

`TERMS_TEXT_VERSION` is `0.1.0` — I confirmed that against QA by reading its privacy pane, which renders `έκδοση 0.1.0`, matching the brief's note that the QA member opted in under terms `0.1.0`. When it and a deployment disagree the page names both numbers and the opt-in won't collect consent. Fixture brands are exempt, or every dev run and preview would refuse for nothing.

1079 tests pass, including one that renders against a real brand directory to prove the drift notice actually fires rather than just compiling.

It says in its own docstring that it isn't counsel-approved drafting. Replacing it with reviewed text is rewriting strings; the version check is what makes that safe.

Next: `join.astro`, the path helper, the wallet band repointed. Then QA for both, since previews are still down.

## What the opt-in actually handles

The second is the one I'd have missed without reading the SQL: a member with `status: "left"` gets the same screen with a different sentence, because the upsert *re-joins* rather than writing a second row. `200 active` says "nothing to do" and points at the wallet rather than redirecting — somebody who followed a link here is owed a reason.

The wallet's band stopped pointing at the catalogue. That was sending members shopping when shopping is precisely what refuses them.

## Two things the tests caught on me

I wrote the route-collision case backwards — asserting `joinPath` and `merchantPath(…, 'join')` *differ*. They're identical strings; that's the whole trade. The failure made me document it properly: Astro resolves the static route first, so a retailer slugged `join` becomes unreachable rather than standing where the opt-in should.

And the rules survey killed a clause I'd drafted for the terms: **click expiry doesn't exist**. `Matcher.Match` has no time predicate. Offers expire, network query windows exist, attribution has no bound. A terms page is the wrong place to invent one.

## Verification status — not done yet

QA is mid-deploy and currently 502 on `/healthz`. The web is still on `main-70ad3ab`, which predates both PRs. A watcher is running for the terms page to appear.

One thing worth flagging: I briefly saw `/el/terms` return **200 serving 404 content**, which looked like a soft-404 bug. It wasn't — re-testing gives a consistent 404, so it was a Cloudflare cache artifact. Mentioning it because I nearly filed it.

Once it lands I'll walk the whole journey signed in: wallet → band → opt-in → accept → confirm the band disappears and a click-out is no longer refused. That's the member path end to end, and it's the first time it will have existed.

Remaining after that: **F4** (catalogue paging), **F5** (per-status click-out copy, all bands clickable, plus the open redirect in the click-out endpoint), **F6** (the wallet's `?entry=` bug and its capped count), then **F1.4/F8** for the browser test.

All 13 clauses render on QA, and the version line reads `0.1.0` with **no drift notice** — the prediction I made from QA's privacy pane held.

## Verified on QA (`main-dd7bfc4`)

The terms page is live and correct: 13 clause headings in order, the referenced list items (tracking steps, void reasons) rendering, no fixture notice (QA has a real brand), and the version line matching the text. That last one is the check I was most unsure about — if I'd guessed wrong, the opt-in would have refused every member on arrival.

## But I can't verify the journey end to end, and the reason matters

**QA is serving two different builds simultaneously.** Correlated probes:

```
terms=404  version=main-70ad3ab     ← old build, no terms page
terms=404  version=main-70ad3ab
terms=502  version=main-dd7bfc4     ← container swapping
terms=200  version=main-dd7bfc4     ← new build
terms=200  version=main-dd7bfc4
...then back to 404/main-70ad3ab
```

`cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC` throughout and cache-busters make no difference, so this is the origin, not Cloudflare. It isn't a rolling deploy settling — it oscillates.

A single-request check works if I retry until I land on the new build. **A multi-step journey doesn't**: sign in → wallet → join → accept is four requests, each landing on a coin-flip build, and the old one has no `/join` route at all.

So I've verified the two pages; I have **not** verified the member journey, and I'm not going to claim otherwise. This looks like the same unwell deployment machinery behind the 502 previews — I'll leave it alone as you asked, but it's now blocking QA verification too, which is worth knowing since it's the only lane left.

## Where F3 leaves the product

A member can sign up → sign in → become an account → read the terms → opt in → click out. That's the whole path to a tracked click, and it exists for the first time.

## Next, unless you'd rather redirect me

**F5's endpoint defects first** — there's a real one in `web/src/pages/api/cashback/clickout.ts`: the failure path does `back.startsWith('/')`, which admits `//evil.example`. That's an open redirect, and this repo already owns the correct check (`safeReturnPath`, written for exactly this in #564). Same PR fixes `createCashbackApi` sitting outside the `try`, which throws a raw 500 at a member mid-click on a misconfigured prod.

Then F5's per-status click-out copy (a 403 now means "not opted in" and should point at the screen I just built), F4's paging, and F6's `?entry=` bug.

I'll re-check the journey on QA once the deploy settles.

input.content:
# F5 — the click-out, end to end

## Context

F3 landed (#590, #593), so a member can sign up, sign in, become an account,
read the terms and opt in. The click-out is the next thing they do, and it is
where the product becomes money — the click is the row every later credit is
attributed to.

Two problems stand between here and that working properly, and they are
different in kind, so they are different PRs.

**One is a defect.** `web/src/pages/api/cashback/clickout.ts` carries an open
redirect on its failure path. Verified still present on `main` today.

**The other is that the screen cannot say what went wrong.** The Go handler
distinguishes six refusals; the page collapses all of them into one sentence.
One of those six is now *actionable* — B3 (#568) made a click-out from a
member who has not opted in answer **403**, and there is finally a screen to
send them to.

### Done, and off this plan

F3 in full: `/{lang}/terms` and the opt-in, both merged and both verified on
QA (`main-dd7bfc4`) — 13 clauses rendering, the version line reading `0.1.0`
with no drift notice. Earlier: the contract correction, the session work,
sign-in, account provisioning, gating, `.mcp.json`, and the stale-issue sweep
(143 open → 99).

---

## PR 1 — the click-out endpoint's own defects

`web/src/pages/api/cashback/clickout.ts`, three of them, smallest first.

**The open redirect.** Line 52:

```ts
const target = typeof back === 'string' && back.startsWith('/') ? back : '/';
return redirect(`${target}?clickout=${status}`, 303);
```

`//evil.example` starts with a slash, is protocol-relative, and leaves the
site. This repository already owns the correct check — `safeReturnPath` in
`web/src/lib/member/access.ts`, written for exactly this in #564, which
rejects `//host`, `/\host`, control characters and over-long values. Use it
rather than write a second one.

**A raw 500 mid-click.** `createCashbackApi` sits *outside* the `try` (line
38). On a deployment with `APP_ENV=prod` and no `API_BASE_URL` it throws
`CashbackConfigurationError` straight out of the route — an Astro error page
to somebody who pressed "open the shop", rather than a redirect back with a
status. Move it inside.

**A malformed query.** `` `${target}?clickout=${status}` `` appends `?`
unconditionally. `back` carries no query today, so it works; the moment it
does, it builds `…?a=1?clickout=409`. Build the URL properly.

No new copy, no new behaviour a member can see except not being sent to
another site. Independently mergeable.

## PR 2 — a refusal a member can act on

### Read the status, not merely its presence

`[slug].astro:97` is `searchParams.has('clickout')`, so the value is
discarded and `t.clickoutFailed` answers for everything. Each of the six
wants a different move:

| Status | The api's own words | What the page should offer |
|---|---|---|
| **403** | *"you have not opted into cashback; accept the terms…"* | **the opt-in screen** — `joinPath(lang, slugs)`, which now exists |
| 429 | the click rule, with `Retry-After` | wait, and say roughly how long |
| 409 | the band expired or the retailer went inactive | the offer is gone; reload to see what is left |
| 502 | *"nothing has been recorded, so trying again later is safe"* | say exactly that — it is the reassuring half |
| 401 | no session | the fence owns this; belt and braces |
| 400 | a bad offer id | ours, not theirs |

An unrecognised value renders nothing, the way `signin.astro` ignores an
outcome it has no sentence for.

### Carry the `Retry-After` through

The Go handler sets it in seconds; the web endpoint drops it, so only the
number `429` survives. `CashbackApiError` carries the status and not the
headers, so this is a small chain — the error learns the header, the endpoint
forwards it, the page renders "in about a minute" rather than "wait a
moment". Its own commit, so the PR is reviewable without it.

### Every published band gets a button

`[slug].astro:105` is `merchant?.rates[0]`, so a retailer publishing two
bands has one a member cannot click **at all**, while the rate table at 170
renders every one of them. Each row carries its own `offer_id`.

The shape: keep the primary call to action, and give each *additional* band
its own small submit inside the table. A retailer with one band looks exactly
as it does now, which is nearly all of them; a retailer with two stops hiding
one. One form, `<button name="offer_id" value={rate.offer_id}>` per band —

## Context

F3 landed (#590, #593), so a member can sign up, sign in, become an account,
read the terms and opt in. The click-out is the next thing they do, and it is
where the product becomes money — the click is the row every later credit is
attributed to.

Two problems stand between here and that working properly, and they are
different in kind, so they are different PRs.

**One is a defect.** `web/src/pages/api/cashback/clickout.ts` carries an open
redirect on its failure path. Verified still present on `main` today.

**The other is that the screen cannot say what went wrong.** The Go handler
distinguishes six refusals; the page collapses all of them into one sentence.
One of those six is now *actionable* — B3 (#568) made a click-out from a
member who has not opted in answer **403**, and there is finally a screen to
send them to.

### Done, and off this plan

F3 in full: `/{lang}/terms` and the opt-in, both merged and both verified on
QA (`main-dd7bfc4`) — 13 clauses rendering, the version line reading `0.1.0`
with no drift notice. Earlier: the contract correction, the session work,
sign-in, account provisioning, gating, `.mcp.json`, and the stale-issue sweep
(143 open → 99).

---

## PR 1 — the click-out endpoint's own defects

`web/src/pages/api/cashback/clickout.ts`, three of them, smallest first.

**The open redirect.** Line 52:

```ts
const target = typeof back === 'string' && back.startsWith('/') ? back : '/';
return redirect(`${target}?clickout=${status}`, 303);
```

`//evil.example` starts with a slash, is protocol-relative, and leaves the
site. This repository already owns the correct check — `safeReturnPath` in
`web/src/lib/member/access.ts`, written for exactly this in #564, which
rejects `//host`, `/\host`, control characters and over-long values. Use it
rather than write a second one.

**A raw 500 mid-click.** `createCashbackApi` sits *outside* the `try` (line
38). On a deployment with `APP_ENV=prod` and no `API_BASE_URL` it throws
`CashbackConfigurationError` straight out of the route — an Astro error page
to somebody who pressed "open the shop", rather than a redirect back with a
status. Move it inside.

unconditionally. `back` carries no query today, so it works; the moment it
does, it builds `…?a=1?clickout=409`. Build the URL properly.

another site. Independently mergeable.

## PR 2 — a refusal a member can act on

### Read the status, not merely its presence

`[slug].astro:97` is `searchParams.has('clickout')`, so the value is
discarded and `t.clickoutFailed` answers for everything. Each of the six
wants a different move:

# F5 — the click-out, end to end

## Context

F3 landed (#590, #593), so a member can sign up, sign in, become an account,
read the terms and opt in. The click-out is the next thing they do, and it is
where the product becomes money — the click is the row every later credit is
attributed to.

Two problems stand between here and that working properly, and they are
different in kind, so they are different PRs.

**One is a defect.** `web/src/pages/api/cashback/clickout.ts` carries an open
redirect on its failure path. Verified still present on `main` today.

**The other is that the screen cannot say what went wrong.** The Go handler
distinguishes six refusals; the page collapses all of them into one sentence.
One of those six is now *actionable* — B3 (#568) made a click-out from a
member who has not opted in answer **403**, and there is finally a screen to
send them to.

### Done, and off this plan

F3 in full: `/{lang}/terms` and the opt-in, both merged and both verified on
QA (`main-dd7bfc4`) — 13 clauses rendering, the version line reading `0.1.0`
with no drift notice. Earlier: the contract correction, the session work,
sign-in, account provisioning, gating, `.mcp.json`, and the stale-issue sweep
(143 open → 99).

---

## PR 1 — the click-out endpoint's own defects

`web/src/pages/api/cashback/clickout.ts`, three of them, smallest first.

**The open redirect.** Line 52:

```ts
const target = typeof back === 'string' && back.startsWith('/') ? back : '/';
return redirect(`${target}?clickout=${status}`, 303);
```

`//evil.example` starts with a slash, is protocol-relative, and leaves the
site. This repository already owns the correct check — `safeReturnPath` in
`web/src/lib/member/access.ts`, written for exactly this in #564, which
rejects `//host`, `/\host`, control characters and over-long values. Use it
rather than write a second one.

**A raw 500 mid-click.** `createCashbackApi` sits *outside* the `try` (line
38). On a deployment with `APP_ENV=prod` and no `API_BASE_URL` it throws
`CashbackConfigurationError` straight out of the route — an Astro error page
to somebody who pressed "open the shop", rather than a redirect back with a
status. Move it inside.

**A malformed query.** `` `${target}?clickout=${status}` `` appends `?`
unconditionally. `back` carries no query today, so it works; the moment it
does, it builds `…?a=1?clickout=409`. Build the URL properly.

No new copy, no new behaviour a member can see except not being sent to
another site. Independently mergeable.

## PR 2 — a refusal a member can act on

### Read the status, not merely its presence

`[slug].astro:97` is `searchParams.has('clickout')`, so the value is
discarded and `t.clickoutFailed` answers for everything. Each of the six
wants a different move:

| Status | The api's own words | What the page should offer |
|---|---|---|
| **403** | *"you have not opted into cashback; accept the terms…"* | **the opt-in screen** — `joinPath(lang, slugs)`, which now exists |
| 429 | the click rule, with `Retry-After` | wait, and say roughly how long |
| 409 | the band expired or the retailer went inactive | the offer is gone; reload to see what is left |
| 502 | *"nothing has been recorded, so trying again later is safe"* | say exactly that — it is the reassuring half |
| 401 | no session | the fence owns this; belt and braces |
| 400 | a bad offer id | ours, not theirs |

An unrecognised value renders nothing, the way `signin.astro` ignores an
outcome it has no sentence for.

### Carry the `Retry-After` through

The Go handler sets it in seconds; the web endpoint drops it, so only the
number `429` survives. `CashbackApiError` carries the status and not the
headers, so this is a small chain — the error learns the header, the endpoint
forwards it, the page renders "in about a minute" rather than "wait a
moment". Its own commit, so the PR is reviewable without it.

### Every published band gets a button

`[slug].astro:105` is `merchant?.rates[0]`, so a retailer publishing two
bands has one a member cannot click **at all**, while the rate table at 170
renders every one of them. Each row carries its own `offer_id`.

The shape: keep the primary call to action, and give each *additional* band
its own small submit inside the table. A retailer with one band looks exactly
as it does now, which is nearly all of them; a retailer with two stops hiding
one. One form, `<button name="offer_id" value={rate.offer_id}>` per band —
the button carries the value, so there is no hidden input per row and no
form-per-row nesting inside a table.

### What this deliberately does *not* do

**No pre-flight `participation()` call on the merchant page.** My earlier plan
said the page should refuse to render the button for a member who has not
opted in. That costs a round trip on *every* merchant page render to save one
wasted click by the minority who have not joined — and after this PR the
wasted click ends in a sentence naming the remedy and a link to it. Letting
them click and telling them is cheaper and no less clear.

---

## Files

- `web/src/pages/api/cashback/clickout.ts` — the three defects, then the
  `Retry-After` forward
- `web/src/pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/[slug].astro` — the status branch and
  the per-band buttons
- `web/src/i18n/cashback.ts` — five new sentences beside `clickoutFailed`, in
  `el` and `de`
- `web/src/lib/cashback/api.ts` — `CashbackApiError` learns `retryAfter`

Reused rather than rewritten: `safeReturnPath`
(`lib/member/access.ts`), `joinPath` (`lib/cashback/paths.ts`), `isSameOrigin`
(`lib/csrf.ts`), and `t.clickoutFailed` as the fallback for a status with no
sentence of its own.

## Verification

```sh
cd web && npm run check && npm test && npm run build
sh scripts/lint-brand-literals.sh          # on a clean worktree
sh scripts/lint-refs.sh "$(git branch --show-current)"
sh scripts/lint-refs.sh --from-messages origin/main..HEAD
sh scripts/lint-commit-authors.sh origin/main..HEAD
```

`pages/api/cashback/clickout.ts` has **no test today**. It gets one: the
container renders an `APIRoute` through its exported `POST`, so the cases are
a cross-origin refusal, a missing `offer_id`, and — the one that matters —
that `back=//evil.example` redirects to `/` and never off-site.

`[slug].astro` has no rendered-page test either. It gets one on the
`wallet.test.ts` pattern, covering the six statuses and a retailer with two
bands offering two buttons.

Then QA, when the deployment settles: open a retailer signed in but not opted
in, press the button, and land back with the sentence and the link to the
opt-in — the loop F3 and F5 close together.

## One caveat carried forward

**QA is currently serving two builds at once.** Correlated probes alternate
between `main-70ad3ab` (no terms page, 404) and `main-dd7bfc4` (200), with
`cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC` throughout and cache-busters making no difference —
so it is the origin, not Cloudflare. Single-request checks work by retrying
until the new build answers; a multi-step journey does not, because each
request lands on a coin-flip. Someone else is on the deployment machinery;
this is only a note that end-to-end verification is unreliable until it
settles.

F5 is done and merged. Now the graft number you asked for.

## Graft: ~2.50M tokens reported, and I'd discount most of it

| Where | Reported |
|---|---|
| Enforced-cashback-rules survey | **~2,411,100** (22 calls) |
| Auth/session survey | **~86,008** |
| Catalogue/click-out/wallet survey | ~0 — *"the task named every file to read"* |
| Shell-exchange survey | ~0 — *"direct reads were the shorter path"* |
| Four other surveys | no tally emitted |
| **Me, directly** | **zero — I still haven't called a graft tool** |

**The honest reading:** that 2.4M is graft's own estimate of what reading every matched file in full would have cost. It is not 2.4M tokens of budget we'd otherwise have spent — nobody would have read those files whole. Treat it as "the graph answered 22 questions that would each have meant opening several large Go files", which is real but not two-and-a-half million real.

The **~86k** figure is the defensible one: that agent genuinely didn't know where the auth seam lived and graft found it.

And the pattern from the zeros is the useful lesson: **graft earns its keep when you don't know where the code is.** Once I'd located things and could name exact files in a prompt, it added nothing — which is why the later surveys report ~0 and aren't failures.

Still true that I use `git grep`/`git log` where `graft callers` would be better. It's now in `.mcp.json` for every session (#582), so the tool is there; the habit isn't yet.

## F5 shipped — [#597](https://github.com/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/pull/597) and [#599](https://github.com/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/pull/599)

**The open redirect is closed.** `back.startsWith('/')` accepted `//evil.example`. The irony is that the route's docstring reasoned carefully about the redirect *out* — "the member never supplies a URL, so there is no open redirect to close" — and nobody looked at the way back. It had **no test at all**, which is how three defects survived in twenty lines under a docstring about being careful.

**The F3/F5 loop is closed.** Press "open the shop" without having opted in, and you now land back with a sentence and a button to the opt-in screen. Previously all six refusals rendered one message that described only one of them.

**A rate nobody could earn.** The page opened `rates[0]` and only that, while the table beside it rendered every band. And **no fixture retailer had two bands**, so it looked correct in every preview and every test. The fixtures now carry one, with a guard case that fails loudly if that's ever removed — otherwise the multi-band test would pass by rendering nothing.

Three of my own assertions failed during this and all three were mine, not the code's — including asserting two paths *differ* when being identical is the entire point of the trade.

## Where things stand

The member journey is complete end to end: sign up → sign in → account → terms → opt in → click out, with every refusal saying what to do.

Left: **F4** (catalogue paging — `next_cursor` discarded, count capped at 20), **F6** (the wallet's `?entry=` resolving against page one only — a correctness bug), then **F1.4/F8** for the browser test. Plus `Retry-After` forwarding, which I deliberately left out of #599 rather than smuggle in.

Still unverified in a browser: QA was serving two builds simultaneously last I checked. I'll retry once it settles.

content.text:
Both good questions. The first one is worse than "missing tags."

## 1. The release pipeline has never succeeded

| Fact | |
|---|---|
| Tags in the repo | **1** — `v0.1.0`, annotated, 2026-08-16 |
| Commits since | **1072** |
| Release workflow runs, ever | **5** — all on 2026-08-16, **all failed** |
| Where they failed | the `release` job, step **"Deploy to Cloudflare"** |
| Staging URL | *empty* |
| Production URL | *empty* |

So it isn't that someone forgot to tag. **The one tag that was cut never released**, five attempts failed at a Cloudflare deploy step, and nobody has tried since. That's three weeks and 1072 commits ago — and the Cloudflare Worker that step targeted has since been *retired* in favour of Caddy (`snippets.caddy` says it "replaces the path routing that `deploy/cloudflare/routing.js` did"). The pipeline is almost certainly still pointed at infrastructure that no longer exists.

Meanwhile QA works fine because it doesn't use this path at all — `publish.yml` stamps `main-<sha>` on every merge to `main`, which is why QA is current and staging and prod are nowhere.

**Why this matters more than it looks.** `RELEASING.md` says the path to production is the one staging has already rehearsed. Nothing has rehearsed anything. There's no rollback point other than a 3-week-old artifact, no changelog for 1072 commits, and — the real risk — the first time anyone needs this to work will be under deadline pressure, against a 7-step pipeline that has never once run green.

**Concretely, and cheaply:** `release.yml` has a `workflow_dispatch` with `dry_run: true` as the default, described as *"verify and stamp everything; move no channel and publish nothing."* That rehearses the whole thing with no staging and no risk. If it fails — and I'd expect the Cloudflare step to — you find out now rather than in October. I'd do that before cutting any tag, and I'm happy to run it and fix what falls out.

## 2. Microservices — too soon, and one reason is close to disqualifying

The short answer is too soon. But the strongest argument isn't team size, it's your database.

**The money invariants are enforced in Postgres, across module lines.** `entry_currency_is_the_members` is a foreign key from `cashback.entry` into `cashback.participation`. `payout.approved_by` is `NOT NULL` referencing `public.account`, with a trigger checking that account holds the operator role. Migration 0014's own comment: *"a payout with no named approver is unrepresentable, not merely rejected by a service."*

Split cashback from identity and **every one of those becomes application code you have to trust.** The constitution's Principle VIII says application code is never trusted with a legal guarantee. Microservices would require abandoning that, which is a much bigger decision than a deployment topology.

**You already have the good half.** `internal/platform/{brand,config,db,events,http,logging,money,scheduler,text}` *is* the shared-boundaries layer you're describing — auth, telemetry, events, money — as libraries rather than services. And `internal/arch/` enforces the boundaries with tests: `TestNetworkAdaptersAreSealed` proves adding a second network adapter changes no file outside its package. That's the discipline microservices are usually adopted to *impose*, already imposed, at compile time, for free.

**And the timing is against it.** Previews are 502, QA served two builds simultaneously an hour ago, and the release pipeline has never worked. Microservices multiply deployment surface by N. Splitting now would multiply the exact thing that is currently your weakest component.

**When it stops being too soon** — worth writing down so it isn't a vibe:
- more than one person deploying, wanting independent cadence
- a component with a genuinely different scaling or availability profile
- a boundary where a database-enforced invariant genuinely doesn't cross

That last one already has a candidate: **the network pollers**. They're scheduler jobs doing outbound I/O on a timer, they don't hold the money invariants, and they'd be a separate deployable without a foreign key crossing the line. If you ever want to prove out a split, that's the piece — not news-vs-cashback.

My recommendation: **fix the release pipeline first.** It's a concrete blocker on the 1 October pilot; the architecture question isn't. And keep the arch tests honest — they're what preserves the option to split later, cheaply.

Want me to run the dry-run release and dig into the Cloudflare failure?

content.text:
I went in with the browser. The journey can't be completed, and here's exactly why.

## The api is down

`healthz`, `readyz` and every cashback route: **502, five out of five**. The web container is up and serving pages; the api behind it is not. Nothing in the member journey works without it.

## Two builds are still being served at once

The clearest evidence from this session: `/el/terms` rendered the **new** build correctly, while `/el/munich/cashback/join` in the very next navigation hit the **old** one — footer `main-70ad3ab`, page title "Καταστήματα", because on that build `/join` isn't a route and falls through to `[slug].astro` with `slug="join"`.

I'd hoped a browser's keep-alive would pin it to one backend. It doesn't. A four-step journey lands on a coin-flip each time, and half those flips land on a build with no opt-in screen.

## What I did verify

**[#590](https://github.com/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/pull/590), the terms page — confirmed visually.** Screenshot: `screenshot-1788817851997-6.jpg`. Two-column layout, clause headings in accent uppercase, the tracking steps and void reasons as lists, the language switcher, and the version line reading **`ΑΥΤΟΙ ΟΙ ΟΡΟΙ ΕΙΝΑΙ Η ΕΚΔΟΣΗ 0.1.0.`** — no drift notice, so the deployment's brand and the text agree, which was the risky prediction.

It also renders *while the api is down*, because it needs no api. That's the design working.

**[#573](https://github.com/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/pull/573)'s error handling — verified under a real outage I didn't stage.** With the api returning 502, the wallet shows:

> *Αυτή η σελίδα δεν μπορεί να φορτώσει αυτή τη στιγμή. Δοκίμασε ξανά σε λίγο.*

That's `pageUnavailable`, the member-facing string I added. Before #573 this would have been `emptyQueue` — "nothing open in this list", an operator's sentence about a work queue — under a 503. A member now gets told the page can't load and to try again, which is true and actionable. I could not have arranged a better test than a genuine outage.

## What's blocked

The journey itself: wallet → band → opt-in → accept → click-out. Every step needs the api. Nothing about it is code-blocked — it's blocked on a QA that has no api process and serves two web builds.

You said the deployment topology is a separate session, so I'll leave it. But the practical consequence is worth stating plainly: **with previews 502 and QA in this state, there is currently no environment where the member journey can be verified.** Unit tests are at 1135 passing, and they cannot substitute for it — that's precisely what the sign-in bug you found taught us.

I'll retry the moment the api answers. Meanwhile F4 (catalogue paging) and F6 (the wallet's `?entry=` correctness bug) are both unblocked and don't need QA to build — want me to carry on with those?

Summary:
## 1. Primary Request and Intent

The user's overarching request: **follow `docs/master-prompts/cashback-frontend.md` thoroughly to produce a complete working cashback frontend**, on the path to "one real transaction" (sign up → opt in → click out → pending wallet entry). Explicit framings across the conversation:

- "you own the designs and experience" — the 26-artboard design canvas artifacts were approved previously
- Backend gaps (B1–B6) are "a to-be-solved issue and not something to be stalled" — build against the documented contract
- "If you reckon there's work you can do in the meantime go ahead and do it"
- **F3 (opt-in + terms): "I'll follow your lead"**
- **F1.4 and F4/F5/F6: "let's plan and act accordingly"**
- **Housekeeping prioritised**: `.mcp.json` must carry *both* graft and IcePanel ("i want them both to be available please, create a small pr for that"); and clean up stale GitHub issues ("I reckon there are many that have been already implemented but where never referenced therefore never closed")

- Two advisory questions: missing semvers (only one 3-week-old tag), and whether to move to monorepo+microservices
- Final instruction: **"go back to the qa testing using claude for chrome you're supposed to do"**

**Standing repo constraints (from CLAUDE.md / constitution — must persist):**
- **Every branch is named `xcoder/<slug>`.** Never `claude/`, `anthropic/`, or any assistant/vendor name.
- **Every commit authored solely by the founder.** Never add `Co-Authored-By` trailers, never mention Claude/Anthropic/AI in commit messages, PR descriptions, code comments, or documentation. Never add `Claude-Session:` trailers.
- **Every commit must be signed** (SSH signing key configured; commits show `G` good-signature).
- Conventional Commits referencing the issue; one PR per issue; never commit directly to `main`; commit small and often; every intermediate commit must build and pass.

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

- **Astro 7 SSR** (`output: 'server'`, `@astrojs/node` standalone), Vitest 4 with `getViteConfig`, `experimental_AstroContainer` for rendered-page tests
- **Go modular monolith** (`cmd/apivo` + `internal/{cashback,identity,account,platform}`), sqlc, Postgres with trigger/constraint-enforced invariants (C-1..C-10)
- **`@supabase/ssr`** httpOnly cookie sessions; `signInWithOtp` / `verifyOtp` / `exchangeCodeForSession`
- **Session seam**: `WeakMap<Request, Session>`, `rememberSession()` / `sessionOf()`; no `Astro.locals` anywhere
- **Brand system**: `BRAND_DIR` → `brandOnHand({brandDir, appEnv})` → `{brand, source}`; `Document` is `{id, version}` only — **no terms text**
- **i18n**: per-surface catalogues (`i18n/cashback.ts`, `lib/legal/strings.ts`, `lib/faq/strings.ts`, `lib/member/strings.ts`), `READING_LANGUAGES = ['el','de']`, each module carries its own completeness test
- **Brand-literal lint** (`scripts/lint-brand-literals.sh`): per-file ratchet; a file with no budget entry fails on its first hit
- **Coverage allowlist** in `web/vitest.config.ts` — new logic modules must be added or they escape the 80% gate
- **Money**: integer minor units + explicit currency (C-6), never floats
- **Deployment**: Caddy edge, `@api path /api/v1/* /healthz /readyz`; QA = `main-<sha>` on every merge; previews = `pr-<n>` image tags reconciled every 60s

## 3. Files and Code Sections

### Created

**`web/src/lib/member/access.ts`** — return-path validation, the security-critical piece reused everywhere since:

```ts
export function safeReturnPath(raw, fallback = DEFAULT_RETURN_PATH): string {
  if (typeof raw !== 'string' || raw === '' || raw.length > 512) return fallback;
  if (!raw.startsWith('/') || raw.startsWith('//')) return fallback;
  if (raw.includes('\\')) return fallback;
  if (/[\u0000-\u001f\u007f]/.test(raw)) return fallback;
  if (raw === '/auth' || raw.startsWith('/auth/')) return fallback;
  return raw;
}
export const ACCESS_OUTCOMES = ['sent','expired','refused','unconfigured','taken','unmade','signedout'] as const;
```

```ts
export function needsSignIn(authenticated: boolean, fixtures: boolean): boolean {

}
export function cashbackPageLanguage(pathname: string): ReadingLanguage | null {
  const match = /^\/([^/]+)\/[^/]+\/cashback(?:\/|$)/.exec(pathname);
  const lang = match?.[1];
  return lang !== undefined && isReadingLanguage(lang) ? lang : null;
}
export function isUnauthorized(error: unknown): boolean {
  return error instanceof CashbackApiError && (error.status === 401 || error.status === 403);
}
```

**`web/src/lib/account/register.ts`** — `registerAccount(baseUrl, token, fetchImpl)` → `{outcome, account}` where outcome ∈ `registered|existing|email_taken|no_email|unavailable`. **Never throws.**

**`web/src/pages/auth/confirm.ts`** — accepts both `token_hash`+`type` and PKCE `code`; narrows `EMAIL_OTP_TYPES = ['email','magiclink','signup','invite','email_change']` (deliberately excluding `recovery`); calls `registerAccount`; drops session on `email_taken`/`no_email`.

**`web/src/lib/legal/terms.ts`** — `TERMS_TEXT_VERSION = '0.1.0'` (confirmed against QA's privacy pane rendering `έκδοση 0.1.0`); 13 clauses; owns headings + exactly 7 statements, references the rest from `cashbackStrings`.

**`web/src/pages/[lang]/terms.astro`** — legal-family page; drift check `const drifted = !fixture && document !== undefined && document.version !== TERMS_TEXT_VERSION;`

**`web/src/pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/join.astro`** — opt-in, five states (404 / `left` / `active` / 503 / 401), POST handles 409 as success and 400 as "reload"; renders offer unconditionally in fixture mode.

**Tests created**: `access.test.ts`, `gate.test.ts`, `register.test.ts`, `terms.test.ts` (module + page), `join.test.ts`, `clickout.test.ts`, `[slug].test.ts`.

### Modified

**`web/src/lib/cashback/types.ts`** — corrected against Go: `EntryState` = `held|pending|confirmed|reserved|paid|reversed` (no `declined`); `PayoutDestination` = `{destination_id, kind, verified_at, verified_method, created_at}` (no `details`); `Withdrawal` = `{request_id, destination_id, amount, state, requested_at, decided_at, decision_reason, payout_reference}`; added `Collection<T>`, `left_at`, nullable `expires_at`, `country`/`terms`, `merchant_name_language`/`_is_fallback`/`hold_rule`.

**`web/src/middleware.ts`** — added `isAccessPath` and `fenceCashback`:
```ts
const fenceCashback = defineMiddleware((context, next) => {
  const lang = cashbackPageLanguage(context.url.pathname);
  if (lang === null) return next();
  const fixtures = answersFromFixtures(API_BASE_URL, {appEnv: APP_ENV, appVersion: PUBLIC_APP_VERSION});
  if (!needsSignIn(sessionOf(context.request).authenticated, fixtures)) return next();
  const here = `${context.url.pathname}${context.url.search}`;
  return context.redirect(signInPath(lang, { next: here }), 303);
});
```

**`web/src/pages/api/cashback/clickout.ts`** — the open redirect fix:
```ts
const backTo = (status: number): string => {
  const target = new URL(safeReturnPath(typeof back === 'string' ? back : null, '/'), url.origin);
  target.searchParams.set('clickout', String(status));
  return `${target.pathname}${target.search}`;
};
```
plus `createCashbackApi` moved inside the `try`.

**`web/src/pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/[slug].astro`** — per-status refusal chain (403→`joinPath`, 429, 409, 502, 401→signIn, fallback, null for junk) and per-band buttons via `<button name="offer_id" value={rate.offer_id}>`.

**Session rename** (129 identifiers, 28 files): `EditorSession`→`Session`, `NO_EDITOR_SESSION`→`NO_SESSION`, `editorSessionFrom`→`sessionFrom`, `rememberEditorSession`→`rememberSession`, `resolveEditorSession`→`resolveSession`, `editorSession`→`sessionOf`.

Fixed in #584; harness now files a session via `rememberSession`.

- **Heredoc ate backslashes** writing `access.ts` (`'/\\'` → `'/\'`, syntax error). Repaired with python using `chr(92)`.
- **My own wrong assertions** (all caught by the tests): `joinPath !== merchantPath(…,'join')` — they're identical, which is the trade; `not.toContain('Άνοιγμα')` — `shopAtTracking` contains it; `not.toContain('name="offer_id"')` — the primary CTA's hidden input has it; `not.toBe('/')` on fixture clickout — `/` is deliberate so previews never send anyone to a real shop.

**Contract drift (#561)** — `withdraw.astro` rendered `destination.details`, a field the Go handler says "there never will be". Verified against `payout/handlers.go:430-446`, `earnings/state.go`, migration 0013.

**Infinite-redirect risk avoided** — past the fence a 401 means a signed-in member the api doesn't recognise; redirecting would loop. Pages render a band with sign-in as a *choice*.

**Version/text drift** — brand carries version, repo carries words. Copy declares `TERMS_TEXT_VERSION`; mismatch → no accept button. Fixture brands exempt (their version is picked for a test).

**Issue sweep** — 143 → 99 open. Method: `git log --grep='(#N)'` + `git grep '#NNN'` (197 numbers with evidence), since `specs/*/tasks.md` checkboxes proved stale (T001–T006 unchecked but built). 19 closed; 5 deliberately left open (#132 still failing, #206 `/attribute` genuinely missing, #275 23 budget lines remain, #117, #524).

**Ongoing/unresolved**: previews 502 despite successful builds; QA oscillating between two builds (`cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC`, cache-busters ineffective → origin, not Cloudflare); **QA api completely down** (502 on healthz/readyz/all cashback routes); release pipeline never succeeded (5 runs, all failed at "Deploy to Cloudflare", a Worker since retired for Caddy).

# F5 — the click-out, end to end

## Context

F3 landed (#590, #593), so a member can sign up, sign in, become an account,
read the terms and opt in. The click-out is the next thing they do, and it is
where the product becomes money — the click is the row every later credit is
attributed to.

Two problems stand between here and that working properly, and they are
different in kind, so they are different PRs.

**One is a defect.** `web/src/pages/api/cashback/clickout.ts` carries an open
redirect on its failure path. Verified still present on `main` today.

**The other is that the screen cannot say what went wrong.** The Go handler
distinguishes six refusals; the page collapses all of them into one sentence.
One of those six is now *actionable* — B3 (#568) made a click-out from a
member who has not opted in answer **403**, and there is finally a screen to
send them to.

### Done, and off this plan

F3 in full: `/{lang}/terms` and the opt-in, both merged and both verified on
QA (`main-dd7bfc4`) — 13 clauses rendering, the version line reading `0.1.0`
with no drift notice. Earlier: the contract correction, the session work,
sign-in, account provisioning, gating, `.mcp.json`, and the stale-issue sweep
(143 open → 99).

---

## PR 1 — the click-out endpoint's own defects

`web/src/pages/api/cashback/clickout.ts`, three of them, smallest first.

**The open redirect.** Line 52:

```ts
const target = typeof back === 'string' && back.startsWith('/') ? back : '/';
return redirect(`${target}?clickout=${status}`, 303);
```

`//evil.example` starts with a slash, is protocol-relative, and leaves the
site. This repository already owns the correct check — `safeReturnPath` in
`web/src/lib/member/access.ts`, written for exactly this in #564, which
rejects `//host`, `/\host`, control characters and over-long values. Use it
rather than write a second one.

**A raw 500 mid-click.** `createCashbackApi` sits *outside* the `try` (line
38). On a deployment with `APP_ENV=prod` and no `API_BASE_URL` it throws
`CashbackConfigurationError` straight out of the route — an Astro error page
to somebody who pressed "open the shop", rather than a redirect back with a
status. Move it inside.

**A malformed query.** `` `${target}?clickout=${status}` `` appends `?`
unconditionally. `back` carries no query today, so it works; the moment it
does, it builds `…?a=1?clickout=409`. Build the URL properly.

No new copy, no new behaviour a member can see except not being sent to
another site. Independently mergeable.

## PR 2 — a refusal a member can act on

### Read the status, not merely its presence

`[slug].astro:97` is `searchParams.has('clickout')`, so the value is
discarded and `t.clickoutFailed` answers for everything. Each of the six
wants a different move:

| Status | The api's own words | What the page should offer |
|---|---|---|
| **403** | *"you have not opted into cashback; accept the terms…"* | **the opt-in screen** — `joinPath(lang, slugs)`, which now exists |
| 429 | the click rule, with `Retry-After` | wait, and say roughly how long |
| 409 | the band expired or the retailer went inactive | the offer is gone; reload to see what is left |
| 502 | *"nothing has been recorded, so trying again later is safe"* | say exactly that — it is the reassuring half |
| 401 | no session | the fence owns this; belt and braces |
| 400 | a bad offer id | ours, not theirs |

An unrecognised value renders nothing, the way `signin.astro` ignores an
outcome it has no sentence for.

### Carry the `Retry-After` through

The Go handler sets it in seconds; the web endpoint drops it, so only the
number `429` survives. `CashbackApiError` carries the status and not the
headers, so this is a small chain — the error learns the header, the endpoint
forwards it, the page renders "in about a minute" rather than "wait a
moment". Its own commit, so the PR is reviewable without it.

### Every published band gets a button

`[slug].astro:105` is `merchant?.rates[0]`, so a retailer publishing two
bands has one a member cannot click **at all**, while the rate table at 170
renders every one of them. Each row carries its own `offer_id`.

The shape: keep the primary call to action, and give each *additional* band
its own small submit inside the table. A retailer with one band looks exactly
as it does now, which is nearly all of them; a retailer with two stops hiding
one. One form, `<button name="offer_id" value={rate.offer_id}>` per band —
the button carries the value, so there is no hidden input per row and no
form-per-row nesting inside a table.

### What this deliberately does *not* do

**No pre-flight `participation()` call on the merchant page.** My earlier plan
said the page should refuse to render the button for a member who has not
opted in. That costs a round trip on *every* merchant page render to save one
wasted click by the minority who have not joined — and after this PR the
wasted click ends in a sentence naming the remedy and a link to it. Letting
them click and telling them is cheaper and no less clear.

---

## Files

- `web/src/pages/api/cashback/clickout.ts` — the three defects, then the
  `Retry-After` forward
- `web/src/pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/[slug].astro` — the status branch and
  the per-band buttons
- `web/src/i18n/cashback.ts` — five new sentences beside `clickoutFailed`, in
  `el` and `de`
- `web/src/lib/cashback/api.ts` — `CashbackApiError` learns `retryAfter`

Reused rather than rewritten: `safeReturnPath`
(`lib/member/access.ts`), `joinPath` (`lib/cashback/paths.ts`), `isSameOrigin`
(`lib/csrf.ts`), and `t.clickoutFailed` as the fallback for a status with no
sentence of its own.

## Verification

```sh
cd web && npm run check && npm test && npm run build
sh scripts/lint-brand-literals.sh          # on a clean worktree
sh scripts/lint-refs.sh "$(git branch --show-current)"
sh scripts/lint-refs.sh --from-messages origin/main..HEAD
sh scripts/lint-commit-authors.sh origin/main..HEAD
```

`pages/api/cashback/clickout.ts` has **no test today**. It gets one: the
container renders an `APIRoute` through its exported `POST`, so the cases are
a cross-origin refusal, a missing `offer_id`, and — the one that matters —
that `back=//evil.example` redirects to `/` and never off-site.

`[slug].astro` has no rendered-page test either. It gets one on the
`wallet.test.ts` pattern, covering the six statuses and a retailer with two
bands offering two buttons.

Then QA, when the deployment settles: open a retailer signed in but not opted
in, press the button, and land back with the sentence and the link to the
opt-in — the loop F3 and F5 close together.

## One caveat carried forward

**QA is currently serving two builds at once.** Correlated probes alternate
between `main-70ad3ab` (no terms page, 404) and `main-dd7bfc4` (200), with
`cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC` throughout and cache-busters making no difference —
so it is the origin, not Cloudflare. Single-request checks work by retrying
until the new build answers; a multi-step journey does not, because each
request lands on a coin-flip. Someone else is on the deployment machinery;
this is only a note that end-to-end verification is unreliable until it
settles.
